The Definitive Fine-Tuning Guide for 3D Generation Models</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://huggingface.co/blog/assets/3d-lora-finetuning/thumbnail.gif" alt="The Definitive Fine-Tuning Guide for 3D Generation Models" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>TLDR; In this blog, we provide fine-tuning scripts and containers to fine-tune TRELLIS.2, a popular 3D model on your 3D assets, that can run both locally and on Hugging Face Jobs. If you are interested in fine-tuning, you can use our scripts with few arguments (assuming you updated your dataset to Hugging Face Hub) or tinker with them yourself with this repository. If you want to learn more, we go through how the script works. Let’s go!</p> <p>3D generation has many uses in robotics, simulation, media, and entertainment. In these fields, it is difficult to make generated objects obey strict rules and standardize model and data representations. There are many file formats, such as GLB and PLY. There are also many representations, such as neural radiance fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS). Each one has different advantages and disadvantages.</p> <p>TRELLIS introduced a common internal representation, called a unified latent representation. Its decoders convert this representation into 3D models in the required output format. Thus, you do not have to use different models for each representation format.</p> <p>The same team then released TRELLIS.2, which improves the model's representation of 3D structure. But neither model gives an easy way to adapt it to a specific task.</p> <p>A general-purpose model, such as TRELLIS.2, can make errors in details that are important for a specific application. For example, a user may need accurate geometry for furniture models. Without fine-tuning for that task, the pretrained model can produce geometry that is insufficiently accurate. We use a subset of GSO that has 188 footwear objects for our experiment. In our initial tests, the pretrained model usually produced shoes that looked correct, but the soles were incorrect. We test whether a LoRA can make the soles more accurate.</p> <p>Our goal is to use the Google Scanned Objects (GSO) dataset to improve the performance of TRELLIS.2 on a specific object category. We will explain which pipeline components to fine-tune and which to leave unchanged during training. The pipeline separates structure, detailed geometry, and materials. Thus, we will fine-tune only the components that are important for our task.</p> <p>Choosing what to freeze matters as much as choosing what to fine-tune.</p> <p>LoRA, short for low-rank adaptation, fine-tunes a model by training small adapter matrices while keeping the original weights frozen. This reduces the number of trainable parameters and the memory needed for their gradients and optimizer state. We use Hugging Face’s PEFT library to add and train these adapters. For more information, read our LoRA guide.</p> <p>Hugging Face Jobs runs containerized workloads on cloud hardware. We use it for preprocessing and for training. To use your own GPU instead, see the local Docker commands below. Before you start, make sure that you have:</p> <p>Before we train, let’s look at how TRELLIS.2 generates a 3D object and where we’ll add LoRA adapters.</p> <p>TRELLIS.2 has five main stages: remove the image background, encode the image, predict the coarse structure, generate detailed geometry, and generate materials. The pipeline then exports the result as a textured mesh.</p> <p>First, BiRefNet removes the background from the input image. DINOv3-L then encodes the image into feature tokens. The generation models use these tokens to guide the 3D object.</p> <p>The sparse-structure flow DiT predicts the object's coarse shape. It is a diffusion transformer (DiT) that makes a small latent of size 16³ × 8. A variational autoencoder (VAE) decoder then changes this latent into a 64 × 64 × 64 occupancy grid. Each voxel in the grid shows if that location is part of the object. A voxel is a pixel in three dimensions. We add LoRA adapters to this model because its output guides the geometry stage.</p> <p>O-Voxel is the 3D format of TRELLIS.2. It is a sparse voxel grid. It keeps only the voxels on the object's surface. Each voxel keeps local geometry, such as a mesh vertex, and material attributes. Because the format is small, a CPU changes a mesh into O-Voxel in seconds. A GPU changes O-Voxel back into a mesh in seconds.</p> <p>Structured sparse latents come from TRELLIS. They keep 3D data in sparse tensors, which makes computation faster. The model uses only approximately 10% of the voxels in the grid, so it does not spend compute on empty voxels. Thus, the shape flow DiT and the texture flow DiT are sparse transformers. The sparse-structure flow DiT is a dense transformer.</p> <p>The shape flow DiT uses the occupancy grid and the DINOv3 feature tokens to make a latent. Another VAE decoder then changes this latent into O-Voxel geometry at a resolution of 512 × 512 × 512.</p> <p>We add LoRA adapters to the DiT at this stage because it controls the object's shape.</p> <p>In the last stage, the texture flow DiT uses the shape latent and the DINOv3 features as input. It defines the materials and textures of the geometry's surface. A VAE decoder then changes the latent into base color, metallic, roughness, and alpha values for each voxel. We do not add LoRA adapters to this stage. Our dataset has diffuse color maps, but it lacks the separate material maps this stage needs for training. Also, our problem is the shoe's shape. The base model already makes good colors and textures.</p> <p>Finally, the pipeline combines the geometry and material attributes into a textured mesh and exports it as a GLB file.</p> <p>We add LoRA adapters only to the sparse-structure flow DiT and the shape flow DiT. These DiTs control the object's shape and geometry. We freeze the texture flow DiT to keep its current capabilities.</p> <p>Our dataset contains diffuse color maps that include baked lighting effects. To train the texture flow DiT, we need separate material maps. The color maps in our dataset mix surface color with lighting. Thus, they are not correct targets for this training.</p> <p>If we train the texture flow DiT on these maps, it can learn to show lighting as a surface property. It can also forget what it learned before, a problem called catastrophic forgetting.</p> <p>Our subset has 188 shoes from the 1,030 objects in GSO. For a dataset this small, LoRA is a better choice than full fine-tuning. Full fine-tuning costs much more. It can also overwrite what the model already does well (its learned priors). Our configuration trains approximately 9.3 million adapter parameters in total for both targeted DiTs. We use rank 8 adapters in the attention and feed-forward (MLP) layers of the sparse-structure flow DiT. We use rank 16 adapters in the attention layers of the shape flow DiT. The rank sets the size of the adapter matrices. A higher rank lets the adapter learn more.</p> <p>A 3D model setup can need many dependencies and installation steps. We supply two Docker images (that you can run on Jobs or your own machine) with the necessary software. One image is for preprocessing, and one is for fine-tuning.</p> <p>To train your LoRA adapters and upload them to the Hub:</p> <p>Then we explain the fine-tuning script, its settings, and how each setting affects training.</p> <p>We’ll walk through three parts of the experiment:</p> <p>We save the preprocessed dataset so that all training runs can reuse it.</p> <p>The preprocessing container uses Blender to render 16 views of each object. LoRA training will use these views as conditioning images. Blender runs without a display, through the xvfb-run utility. The container also processes each object through the preprocessing pipeline. See the footwear dataset here for an example intermediate output. For our 188 objects, the full run took approximately 1 hour on an a100-large job. A compact version of the preprocessing pipeline is also available in this companion repository.</p> <p>For Hugging Face Jobs, we pass the following arguments:</p> <p>This container accepts a few more arguments (regardless of being run on Hugging Face Jobs or with Docker), that you can find documented over here. The steps taken in the preprocessing pipeline are documented in this section later.</p> <p>The training container loads the prepared dataset and a configuration preset or file. It records training metrics with Trackio. Use the Trackio dashboard to monitor the run.</p> <p>We use ‘ss’ and ‘shape’ to indicate the two modes we have for training the LoRAs. The ‘ss’ mode will finetune only the Sparse-Structure Flow DiT, whereas the ‘shape’ mode will finetune the Shape Flow DiT. Under the hood, they simply reference different config.json files to use for each stage. More details about the process is available in this section later.</p> <p>If you set --push-to, the container uploads adapter checkpoints to the Hub. The container accepts parameters that are also documented here for brevity. A compact script is also available in the same repository.</p> <p>If you want to play around and fine-tune with the already-processed dataset we have, feel free to use the following set of commands.</p> <p>The commands and flags are the same as for Hugging Face Jobs. Only the Docker options are different.</p> <p>If you want to use our already-preprocessed dataset locally on your machine of choice, use the following commands:</p> <p>Our trained LoRA adapters are in this repository: suvadityamuk/trellis-2-finetune-gso</p> <p>We use TRELLIS.2’s frozen encoders to convert the input meshes into training latents. We save these latents, so later runs do not have to encode the meshes again.</p> <p>We also render 16 views of each object in Blender. During training, we select one random view for each sample as the conditioning image. We keep 9 of the 188 objects for evaluation and train on the other 179. These held-out objects show whether the adapters work on objects unseen by the model during training.</p> <p>Some of the views that Blender rendered for one object</p> <p>The first snippet sets up the data. FLOW selects the flow DiT to train (ss or shape), and STEPS sets the number of optimizer steps. A batch size of 4 with 4 gradient accumulation steps gives an effective batch size of 16. Then, the snippet loads the LoRA config file for the selected flow DiT, makes the dataset in the TRELLIS.2 format, removes the held-out objects, and makes the data loader for fine-tuning.</p> <p>We use the peft library to insert LoRA adapters into the selected layers. TRELLIS.2 has a custom forward pass, so the standard PeftModel() wrapper does not work. Instead, we call inject_adapter_in_model(). This function adds the adapters directly to the model and keeps its custom interface.</p> <p>We keep the trainable adapter weights in 32-bit floating point (fp32) for numerical stability and use bfloat16 (bf16) autocasting for the forward pass. Autocasting lets PyTorch use lower precision for some operations, which decreases memory use. Autocasting does not change how the frozen backbone weights are stored.</p> <p>It’s important to note that our objective function here is good-old rectified flow matching (as seen in popular image-generation models like Stable Diffusion 3, Flux 2, and others). TRELLIS.2 used the same objective in pretraining, so it is a good choice for fine-tuning. For the theory, read this blog about flow matching.</p> <p>We update only the LoRA parameters in the sparse-structure and shape DiTs. All original model weights remain frozen.</p> <p>The snippets below show the core training loop for one stage. They are simpler than the container code and do not include some setup steps. For the full workflow, use the container commands.</p> <p>We initialize the optimizer and load DINOv3 to extract features from the input images.</p> <p>We then follow these steps within the training loop:</p> <p>The training loop computes the loss and updates the adapter weights. Gradient accumulation adds the gradients from 4 small batches before each optimizer step. Gradient checkpointing saves GPU memory by recomputing some intermediate values during backpropagation. The outer loop runs for a given number of optimizer steps, whereas the inner loop accumulates gradients over a set of batches.</p> <p>For each batch, DINOv3 encodes the conditioning image. For classifier-free guidance (CFG) dropout, the loop sets the conditioning to zero for a random fraction (p_uncond) of the samples. Then, it calculates the flow-matching loss with bf16 autocasting. After the inner loop, it clips the gradients to prevent very large updates and does an optimizer step. It logs the loss every 10 steps and saves an adapter checkpoint every 500 steps.</p> <p>We trained two adapters: one for the sparse-structure DiT and one for the shape DiT. The LoRA config files in the container image contain the full training settings: ss_flow_lora_gso.json for the sparse-structure flow DiT and slat_flow_img2shape_lora_gso.json for the shape flow DiT. Each run used one A100 80 GB on Hugging Face Jobs. The sparse-structure run took 7.2 hours, and the shape run took 3.6 hours.</p> <p>The training loss of the sparse-structure flow DiT falls quickly at the start, then more slowly. The loss of the shape flow DiT stays at approximately the same level. These curves show how the training objective changes, but they do not directly measure the quality of the generated geometry.</p> <p>Flow-matching loss varies with the sampled objects, noise, and timesteps. To find out if fine-tuning improves the geometry, we must also compare outputs on the held-out objects.</p> <p>The figure below compares outputs for five of the nine held-out objects. It shows the input image, the base model’s generated output, the base output after a rotation adjustment, the output with the footwear adapters, and the reference scan. In these examples, the soles from the fine-tuned model are closer to the scans.</p> <p>We also use three metrics to evaluate the geometry on the test set:</p> <p>In the chart’s nine-object comparison, the base model has a mean F-score of 0.276, compared with 0.803 for the model with the footwear adapters. Chamfer distance falls from 0.174 to 0.033, and normal consistency rises from 0.530 to 0.804. With both adapters, the F-score is better on all nine held-out objects.</p> <p>For the statistics of all runs, see this Trackio space.</p> <p>Phew, so there we go! We fine-tuned TRELLIS.2 for footwear generation by adding LoRA adapters to the two model components that control geometry. We prepared the data once, trained the adapters in separate jobs, and evaluated the outputs on held-out objects.</p> <p>The main lesson is to select a training target that agrees with the problem and the data that you have. For this experiment, we fine-tuned the structure and shape stages and froze the texture stage.</p> <p>Next, we can examine if the same choices help other 3D generation models, such as Pixal3D and UniLat3D.</p> <p>Gaussian-splat and world-generation models, such as HunyuanWorld 2.0 and NVIDIA Lyra 2.0, are also possible next steps. Their representations and training pipelines can need different methods.</p> <p>Thank you for following along, and see you in the next one! 👋🤗</p> <p>Visualize how noise transforms into images in your browser</p> <p>An interactive guide to 3D representations.</p> <p>Visualize how noise transforms into images in your browser</p> <p>An interactive guide to 3D representations.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/blog/3d-lora-finetuning" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9699"> <h2>#9699. Ahrefs vs SEMrush: Which SEO Tool Should You Use?</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEgjp-Lwdt6oYlgGQ0HWI9cLSBOiniI0CKOWnRWuiQTe2uBJIenevsoZKESvI4-Uo-4r6VU1RjQZUtLtpA1vJyAZhg0fEFn-wOintkjZnNkYcZjS0XIs3XQ2dPgOwKfZZw4YubtvjfJRsVyRBc4tCckB7yip4A-9W1yMbv7bBk3zEGElqHhzHxBdoQAOCg=s1920" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><img alt="semrush vs ahrefs" border="0" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEgjp-Lwdt6oYlgGQ0HWI9cLSBOiniI0CKOWnRWuiQTe2uBJIenevsoZKESvI4-Uo-4r6VU1RjQZUtLtpA1vJyAZhg0fEFn-wOintkjZnNkYcZjS0XIs3XQ2dPgOwKfZZw4YubtvjfJRsVyRBc4tCckB7yip4A-9W1yMbv7bBk3zEGElqHhzHxBdoQAOCg=w640-h360" title="semrush vs ahrefs" width="640" /></span></a></div><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /></span></p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><!--StartFragment--> </span><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12pt;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">SEMrush and Ahrefs are among the most popular tools in the SEO industry. Both companies have been in business for years and have thousands of customers per month.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">If you're a professional SEO or trying to do digital marketing on your own, at some point you'll likely consider using a tool to help with your efforts. Ahrefs and SEMrush are two names that will likely appear on your shortlist.</span></p> <div id="atContainer-8a426783aef805554f3d96c19f8beeb7"></div> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">In this guide, I'm going to help you learn more about these SEO tools and how to choose the one that's best for your purposes.</span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>What is SEMrush?</b></span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"></span></p><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEj19XUpt9Fx6nM7Ny-YihiwJWB3uGFI9tHee_lrhQeIenb_r1q2oBe1dISx7oQMgmqyySFMeVYw5s6BuI5UArx4xk-yedJTPno9GEckbtENs6soBmpzX4VduRbH8V0oZnRFSM-pWh8bHtur90-lgI69vlx5khN1QiHmy1m5SCfSeWjOg2S9szWoIz16Gw=s1660" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><img alt="semrush" border="0" height="350" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEj19XUpt9Fx6nM7Ny-YihiwJWB3uGFI9tHee_lrhQeIenb_r1q2oBe1dISx7oQMgmqyySFMeVYw5s6BuI5UArx4xk-yedJTPno9GEckbtENs6soBmpzX4VduRbH8V0oZnRFSM-pWh8bHtur90-lgI69vlx5khN1QiHmy1m5SCfSeWjOg2S9szWoIz16Gw=w640-h350" title="senrush" width="640" /></a></span></div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span><a name="more"></a></span><b><br /></b></span><p></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">SEMrush is a popular SEO tool with a wide range of features—it's the leading competitor research service for online marketers. SEMrush's SEO Keyword Magic tool offers over 20 billion Google-approved keywords, which are constantly updated and it's the largest keyword database.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The program was developed in 2007 as SeoQuake is a small Firefox extension</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Features</b></span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Most accurate keyword data:</b> Accurate keyword search volume data is crucial for SEO and PPC campaigns by allowing you to identify what keywords are most likely to bring in big sales from ad clicks. SEMrush constantly updates its databases and provides the most accurate data.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Largest Keyword database:</b> SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool now features 20-billion keywords, providing marketers and SEO professionals the largest database of keywords.</span></li> <span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /></span><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">All SEMrush users receive daily ranking data, mobile volume information, and the option to buy additional keywords by default with no additional payment or add-ons needed</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Most accurate position tracking tool: </b>This tool provides all subscribers with basic tracking capabilities, making it suitable for SEO professionals. Plus, the Position Tracking tool provides local-level data to everyone who uses the tool.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>SEO Data Management: </b>SEMrush makes managing your online data easy by allowing you to create visually appealing custom PDF reports, including Branded and White Label reports, report scheduling, and integration with GA, GMB, and GSC.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Toxic link monitoring and penalty recovery: </b>With SEMrush, you can make a detailed analysis of toxic backlinks, toxic scores, toxic markers, and outreach to those sites.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Content Optimization and Creation Tools: </b>SEMrush offers content optimization and creation tools that let you create SEO-friendly content. Some features include the SEO Writing Assistant, On-Page SEO Check, er/SEO Content Template, Content Audit, Post Tracking, Brand Monitoring.</span></li></ul><p></p> <h2 style="margin: 12pt 0in; text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Ahrefs</span></h2><div><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEiFPt6nHmthnZI41Oon-MIy17GEkHvEbLK9v0wD4O6LeObZYb7CJtZjqHTtcjbIYFUX_97R049GK6a7rCS9LfObFMUIchs0V2iFLEs5QJdsj6dtuktGWOV2i4TE69JTj2-HSE5U9Qdgo78OSsCjHsA0Ho9KlNt-odFsCmALTxdCf0B9Rp58lq53mnTYog=s1664" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><img alt="ahrefs" border="0" height="316" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEiFPt6nHmthnZI41Oon-MIy17GEkHvEbLK9v0wD4O6LeObZYb7CJtZjqHTtcjbIYFUX_97R049GK6a7rCS9LfObFMUIchs0V2iFLEs5QJdsj6dtuktGWOV2i4TE69JTj2-HSE5U9Qdgo78OSsCjHsA0Ho9KlNt-odFsCmALTxdCf0B9Rp58lq53mnTYog=w640-h316" title="ahrefs" width="640" /></span></a></div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /><span><!--more--></span><span><br /></span></span></div> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Ahrefs is a leading SEO platform that offers a set of tools to grow your search traffic, research your competitors, and monitor your niche. The company was founded in 2010, and it has become a popular choice among SEO tools. Ahrefs has a keyword index of over 10.3 billion keywords and offers accurate and extensive backlink data updated every 15-30 minutes and it is the world's most extensive backlink index database.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Features</b></span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Backlink alerts data and new keywords</b>: Get an alert when your site is linked to or discussed in blogs, forums, comments, or when new keywords are added to a blog posting about you.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Intuitive interface: </b>The intuitive design of the widget helps you see the overall health of your website and search engine ranking at a glance.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Site Explorer: </b>The Site Explorer will give you an in-depth look at your site's search traffic.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Domain Comparison</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Reports with charts and graphs</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">JavaScript rendering and a site audit can identify SEO issues.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">A question explorer that provides well-crafted topic suggestions</span></li></ul><p></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Direct Comparisons: Ahrefs vs SEMrush</b></span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Now that you know a little more about each tool, let's take a look at how they compare. I'll analyze each tool to see how they differ in interfaces, keyword research resources, rank tracking, and competitor analysis.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>User Interface</b></span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Ahrefs and SEMrush both offer comprehensive information and quick metrics regarding your website's SEO performance. However, Ahrefs takes a bit more of a hands-on approach to getting your account fully set up, whereas SEMrush's simpler dashboard can give you access to the data you need quickly.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">In this section, we provide a brief overview of the elements found on each dashboard and highlight the ease with which you can complete tasks.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>AHREFS</b></span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"></span></p><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEhk3VNx-XZQai3cSSRUZ1EnAPaJfaBIpsLoApcbaYpea06OuGUuNtK87c3vMzo3GW557VsH1Pjafx4WhwJOwFxFQ47gVIiXj7cnEMj9bBsnUztsLE4amuvbAbqG8DhWjTVlv3sEN-YIYzp46pZA7uVzzetGe6BNZTSgwtCePCEqd31bmt8HcoVt44HAJA=s742" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><img alt="ahrefs interface" border="0" height="356" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEhk3VNx-XZQai3cSSRUZ1EnAPaJfaBIpsLoApcbaYpea06OuGUuNtK87c3vMzo3GW557VsH1Pjafx4WhwJOwFxFQ47gVIiXj7cnEMj9bBsnUztsLE4amuvbAbqG8DhWjTVlv3sEN-YIYzp46pZA7uVzzetGe6BNZTSgwtCePCEqd31bmt8HcoVt44HAJA=w640-h356" title="ahrefs interface" width="640" /></a></span></div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /><span><!--more--></span><b><br /></b></span><p></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The Ahrefs dashboard is less cluttered than that of SEMrush, and its primary menu is at the very top of the page, with a search bar designed only for entering URLs.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Additional features of the Ahrefs platform include:</b></span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">You can see analytics from the dashboard, including search engine rankings to domain ratings, referring domains, and backlink</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Jumping from one tool to another is easy. You can use the Keyword Explorer to find a keyword to target and then directly track your ranking with one click.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The website offers a tooltip helper tool that allows you to hover your mouse over something that isn't clear and get an in-depth explanation.</span></li></ul><p></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>SEMRUSH</b></span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"></span></p><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEja9R_j5CeaUWEwdfV8efIiouyrgLKBhy0e4iE4469LObloNet5cUUFz3NdoHbfe7esbgJc-8XoKKjKOB3bscOK31TzJ_EYwF6PdX7Qpmw3RNuJFmViPOG6nuyfWIVPIDwVA0lbdK-8ygQRvhuCanSLXCaHEU0XrKRp9-HhsXf8E7Rs27GvyNzVxztvGw=s1668" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><img alt="semrush domain overview" border="0" height="348" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEja9R_j5CeaUWEwdfV8efIiouyrgLKBhy0e4iE4469LObloNet5cUUFz3NdoHbfe7esbgJc-8XoKKjKOB3bscOK31TzJ_EYwF6PdX7Qpmw3RNuJFmViPOG6nuyfWIVPIDwVA0lbdK-8ygQRvhuCanSLXCaHEU0XrKRp9-HhsXf8E7Rs27GvyNzVxztvGw=w640-h348" title="semrush domain overview" width="640" /></a></span></div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /><span><!--more--></span><b><br /></b></span><p></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">When you log into the SEMrush Tool, you will find four main modules. These include information about your domains, organic keyword analysis, ad keyword, and site traffic.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">You'll also find some other options like</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">A search bar allows you to enter a domain, keyword, or anything else you wish to explore.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">A menu on the left side of the page provides quick links to relevant information, including marketing insights, projects, keyword analytics, and more.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The customer support resources located directly within the dashboard can be used to communicate with the support team or to learn about other resources such as webinars and blogs.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Detailed descriptions of every resource offered. This detail is beneficial for new marketers, who are just starting.</span></li></ul><p></p> <h4 style="margin-bottom: 15.95pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 15.95pt; margin: 15.95pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span color="windowtext">WHO WINS?</span></span></h4> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Both Ahrefs and SEMrush have user-friendly dashboards, but Ahrefs is less cluttered and easier to navigate. On the other hand, SEMrush offers dozens of extra tools, including access to customer support resources.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">When deciding on which dashboard to use, consider what you value in the user interface, and test out both.</span></p> <h3 style="margin-bottom: 14.05pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 14.05pt; margin: 14.05pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span color="windowtext">Rank Tracking</span></span></h3> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">If you're looking to track your website's search engine ranking, rank tracking features can help. You can also use them to monitor your competitors.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Let's take a look at Ahrefs vs. SEMrush to see which tool does a better job.</span></p> <h2 style="margin: 12pt 0in; text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Ahrefs</span></h2><div><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEiwI2EsnhOaR8PPGn03_vC7Rnhyl6hbADM_ilA7IukOAIz0A7SFJDh0Gkj85yqIOJv4gBiiBdfcd_0hy3b7gTYPZhUKQ4eyWLi60IxDA_w-tXRSQ3QkogvhxI1lgvgM59SpOnj8Z6rj9mC_EEBV8k60_c3P4ywhjUD5DKgpM73Vei7qqC7sHIIyVyYXxA=s623" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><img alt="ahrefs rank tracking" border="0" height="506" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEiwI2EsnhOaR8PPGn03_vC7Rnhyl6hbADM_ilA7IukOAIz0A7SFJDh0Gkj85yqIOJv4gBiiBdfcd_0hy3b7gTYPZhUKQ4eyWLi60IxDA_w-tXRSQ3QkogvhxI1lgvgM59SpOnj8Z6rj9mC_EEBV8k60_c3P4ywhjUD5DKgpM73Vei7qqC7sHIIyVyYXxA=w640-h506" title="ahrefs rank tracking" width="640" /></span></a></div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /><span><br /></span></span></div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span><!--more--></span> </span><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The Ahrefs Rank Tracker is simpler to use. Just type in the domain name and keywords you want to analyze, and it spits out a report showing you the search engine results page (SERP) ranking for each keyword you enter.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Rank Tracker looks at the ranking performance of keywords and compares them with the top rankings for those keywords. Ahrefs also offers:</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">You'll see metrics that help you understand your visibility, traffic, average position, and keyword difficulty.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">It gives you an idea of whether a keyword would be profitable to target or not.</span></p> <h4 style="margin-bottom: 15.95pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 15.95pt; margin: 15.95pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span color="windowtext">SEMRUSH</span></span></h4><div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEhcPjF5Xp0f_j3LEzL1aOppWxoqdWtxA7kwRMnWHbiSk-_coyrMwWl6kjy3t_sT0TULSm0C6CzC2-xxgTzz_Gp7zDB5uotawo722P-uBuk_Wm1LXyj3W2zKSGIPRazUBmHLGaFWXskZcQGSezKY5yQF07pKF3QYdWIqXyDoNuSvG9Iv8bnR3-fB29VRSA=s352" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><img alt="semrush position tracking" border="0" height="260" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEhcPjF5Xp0f_j3LEzL1aOppWxoqdWtxA7kwRMnWHbiSk-_coyrMwWl6kjy3t_sT0TULSm0C6CzC2-xxgTzz_Gp7zDB5uotawo722P-uBuk_Wm1LXyj3W2zKSGIPRazUBmHLGaFWXskZcQGSezKY5yQF07pKF3QYdWIqXyDoNuSvG9Iv8bnR3-fB29VRSA=w640-h260" title="semrush position tracking" width="640" /></a></div><br /><span color="windowtext"><br /></span></span><span><!--more--></span></span></div> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">SEMRush offers a tool called Position Tracking. This tool is a project tool—you must set it up as a new project. Below are a few of the most popular features of the SEMrush Position Tracking tool:</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">All subscribers are given regular data updates and mobile search rankings upon subscribing</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The platform provides opportunities to track several SERP features, including Local tracking.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Intuitive reports allow you to track statistics for the pages on your website, as well as the keywords used in those pages.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Identify pages that may be competing with each other using the Cannibalization report.</span></p> <h4 style="margin-bottom: 15.95pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 15.95pt; margin: 15.95pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span color="windowtext">WHO WINS?</span></span></h4> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Ahrefs is a more user-friendly option. It takes seconds to enter a domain name and keywords. From there, you can quickly decide whether to proceed with that keyword or figure out how to rank better for other keywords.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">SEMrush allows you to check your mobile rankings and ranking updates daily, which is something Ahrefs does not offer. SEMrush also offers social media rankings, a tool you won't find within the Ahrefs platform. Both are good which one do you like let me know in the comment.</span></p> <h2 style="margin: 12pt 0in; text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Keyword Research</span></h2> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Keyword research is closely related to rank tracking, but it's used for deciding which keywords you plan on using for future content rather than those you use now.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">When it comes to SEO, keyword research is the most important thing to consider when comparing the two platforms.</span></p> <h4 style="margin-bottom: 15.95pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 15.95pt; margin: 15.95pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span color="windowtext">AHREFS</span></span></h4><div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><div class="separator" style="clear: both; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The Ahrefs Keyword Explorer provides you with thousands of keyword ideas and filters search results based on the chosen search engine.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Ahrefs supports several features, including:</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">It can search multiple keywords in a single search and analyze them together. At SEMrush, you also have this feature in Keyword Overview.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Ahrefs has a variety of keywords for different search engines, including Google, YouTube, Amazon, Bing, Yahoo, Yandex, and other search engines.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">When you click on a keyword, you can see its search volume and keyword difficulty, but also other keywords related to it, which you didn't use.</span></li></ul><p></p> <h2 style="margin: 12pt 0in; text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">SEMRUSH</span></h2><div><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEjiBVN83kj79tj3MmwHM5ELWsU9oAx5bZ7Y7znUE1zevmfGZNcshIh-7WzAWu7StXVuAG7wcLTgAzfLSn5wZ-8ur9EQtkjlMb0Tz22Qitnl1iKHq7iSfq3oNr281qY_3jamHUjaSWx2Yl4Q-47dZmgjLyvO9l9LooPjxRLN2eZTZIT0u8awK8ImaZsaoQ=s1672" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><img border="0" height="346" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEjiBVN83kj79tj3MmwHM5ELWsU9oAx5bZ7Y7znUE1zevmfGZNcshIh-7WzAWu7StXVuAG7wcLTgAzfLSn5wZ-8ur9EQtkjlMb0Tz22Qitnl1iKHq7iSfq3oNr281qY_3jamHUjaSWx2Yl4Q-47dZmgjLyvO9l9LooPjxRLN2eZTZIT0u8awK8ImaZsaoQ=w640-h346" width="640" /></span></a></div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /><span><br /></span></span></div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span><!--more--></span> </span><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool has over 20 billion keywords for Google. You can type in any keyword you want, and a list of suggested keywords will appear.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The Keyword Magic Tool also lets you to:</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Show performance metrics by keyword</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Search results are based on both broad and exact keyword matches.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Show data like search volume, trends, keyword difficulty, and CPC.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Show the first 100 Google search results for any keyword.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Identify SERP Features and Questions related to each keyword</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">SEMrush has released a new Keyword Gap Tool that uncovers potentially useful keyword opportunities for you, including both paid and organic keywords.</span></li></ul><p></p> <h4 style="margin-bottom: 15.95pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 15.95pt; margin: 15.95pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span color="windowtext">WHO WINS?</span></span></h4> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Both of these tools offer keyword research features and allow users to break down complicated tasks into something that can be understood by beginners and advanced users alike.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">If you're interested in keyword suggestions, SEMrush appears to have more keyword suggestions than Ahrefs does. It also continues to add new features, like the Keyword Gap tool and SERP Questions recommendations.</span></p> <h3 style="margin-bottom: 14.05pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 14.05pt; margin: 14.05pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span color="windowtext">Competitor Analysis</span></span></h3> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Both platforms offer competitor analysis tools, eliminating the need to come up with keywords off the top of your head. Each tool is useful for finding keywords that will be useful for your competition so you know they will be valuable to you.</span></p> <h4 style="margin-bottom: 15.95pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 15.95pt; margin: 15.95pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span color="windowtext">AHREFS</span></span></h4><div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEhPVWMffMoYqUU3U1PvQqmOTRNlQmKNSOfvhQ9CU4iIbeICqhQnDrk54c2B_bv_ceqp8JvCdeZ_mhVhMIZM243qpMPJzn1qrFhPmAYs1RQ2U-4jdm5Wml5ByEDhfJSxkqXo2nHegAvrGStAfrx1kADwNhiqzh_ctgmDhaVUrbzu2tvU_9W1rc09LZv-Dw=s768" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span>Ahrefs' domain comparison tool lets you compare up to five websites (your website and four competitors) side-by-side.it also shows you </span>how your site is ranked against others with metrics such as backlinks, domain ratings, and more.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Use the Competing Domains section to see a list of your most direct competitors, and explore how many keywords matches your competitors have.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">To find more information about your competitor, you can look at the Site Explorer and Content Explorer tools and type in their URL instead of yours.</span></p> <h4 style="margin-bottom: 15.95pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 15.95pt; margin: 15.95pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span color="windowtext">SEMRUSH</span></span></h4><div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEjFfBJXtpt_AgR1qT00BIOsWz_HhUEeTLPUsO_FjMCnR4fFAjD2O-_ba6oQoYl3T4Y-PmPD31ZIVieQJTn5r_uX0PQASI6yYAvPBpm7n7YM4wJ9fsBlQ69mU9npFUYxs5-1zJJvZ2--QDrJAvTpIEstcxsyE6sZ3zz36rd35qp6loVAEAvOxmjqZu06rg=s1620" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">SEMrush provides a variety of insights into your competitors' marketing tactics. The platform enables you to research your competitors effectively. It also offers several resources for competitor analysis including:</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Traffic Analytics helps you identify where your audience comes from, how they engage with your site, what devices visitors use to view your site, and how your audiences overlap with other websites.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">SEMrush's Organic Research examines your website's major competitors and shows their organic search rankings, keywords they are ranking for, and even if they are ranking for any (SERP) features and more.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The Market Explorer search field allows you to type in a domain and lists websites or articles similar to what you entered. Market Explorer also allows users to perform in-depth data analytics on These companies and markets.</span></p> <h4 style="margin-bottom: 15.95pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 15.95pt; margin: 15.95pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span color="windowtext">WHO WINS?</span></span></h4> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">SEMrush wins here because it has more tools dedicated to competitor analysis than Ahrefs. However, Ahrefs offers a lot of functionality in this area, too. It takes a combination of both tools to gain an advantage over your competition.</span></p> <h2 style="margin: 12pt 0in; text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Pricing</span></h2> <h3 style="margin: 12pt 0in; Choose the one which meets your requirements and if you have any experience using either Ahrefs or SEMrush let me know in the comment section which works well for you.</span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> </span></p> <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 12.0pt; margin-left: 0in; margin-right: 0in; margin-top: 12.0pt; margin: 12pt 0in;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> </span></p> <!--EndFragment--></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://techncruncher.blogspot.com/2022/03/ahrefs-vs-semrush-which-seo-tool-should.html" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9698"> <h2>#9698. TikTok Shop bundle discounts need a refund-aware contribution ceiling</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://dev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/articles/3otvb2z646ytpt1hl2rv.jpg" alt="TikTok Shop bundle discounts need a refund-aware contribution ceiling" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Bundle promotions often pass a simple gross-margin test and still reduce contribution profit.</p> <p>A "buy two, save 15%" offer may preserve a positive spread between list price and product cost while the platform fee, creator commission, payment fee, shipping subsidy and refund losses consume the rest.</p> <p>What is the largest discount this bundle can take while still meeting a target contribution margin after expected refunds?</p> <p>The model below answers that question with a closed-form ceiling, then validates the answer against settled order data.</p> <p>Use one placed order as the unit of analysis.</p> <p>The effective creator commission rate should reflect attachment, not only the headline rate:</p> <p>For example, 30% attachment at a 12% commission rate gives an effective rate of 3.6%.</p> <p>Use a planning assumption for a new promotion. Use the realised commission field when validating existing orders.</p> <p>Define L as the loss that remains after the platform, payment provider, creator or supplier has reversed whatever is recoverable. It may include:</p> <p>This keeps the refund term honest. A full refund does not necessarily reverse the whole cost of the order.</p> <p>If an order is not refunded, contribution profit is:</p> <p>If it is refunded, the model applies L as the remaining net loss.</p> <p>For a target contribution margin t, require:</p> <p>Solve for minimum acceptable net merchandise revenue:</p> <p>The denominator must be positive. If it is zero or negative, the fee, commission and target-margin rates already consume the full revenue base.</p> <p>The bundle can carry a discount up to about 43.2% under these assumptions and still meet a 15% contribution-margin target after expected refund losses.</p> <p>That result is specific to the inputs. Change the refund loss, attachment rate or fulfilment cost and the ceiling changes.</p> <p>Using the same example, the discount ceiling moves with the target contribution margin:</p> <p>The table makes the trade-off visible to merchandising, finance and growth teams.</p> <p>A 40% discount may be acceptable for a low-cost clearance bundle and unacceptable for a fragile, high-return SKU. The difference belongs in the inputs, not in a blanket sitewide discount policy.</p> <p>The planning formula should be checked against realised contribution for the same discount band.</p> <p>The query below assumes refunds are mature enough to treat net_refund_loss as settled:</p> <p>Treat mixed currencies separately. If discounts changed return behaviour, compare orders created under the same policy window.</p> <p>Only some orders are attached to creators. Use expected attachment for planning and realised commissions for reconciliation.</p> <p>Shipping, payment fees, damaged inventory and non-reversed commission can remain after the customer is refunded.</p> <p>A deep discount can attract customers with a different return profile. Re-estimate r and L by discount band.</p> <p>Platform and payment fees may use discounted merchandise, gross order value or a fixed fee component. Match the actual platform statement.</p> <p>Keep currency, tax and fee boundaries consistent inside one calculation.</p> <p>Orders still inside the refund window are pending. They do not belong in a settled discount-ceiling comparison.</p> <p>Use the free TikTok Shop pricing calculator to test list price, costs and target margin inputs.</p> <p>The TikTok Shop profit calculator helps reconcile order-level contribution.</p> <p>For a broader view of pricing decisions, read the TikTok Shop pricing strategy guide.</p> <p>I work on Starway Global, a TikTok Shop analytics and operations platform. This model is educational and does not guarantee profit, payback or advertising outcomes.</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails. DEV Community © 2016 - 2026.</p> <p>We're a place where coders share, stay up-to-date and grow their careers.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://dev.to/starwayglobalfz/tiktok-shop-bundle-discounts-need-a-refund-aware-contribution-ceiling-1pdd" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9697"> <h2>#9697. OpenAI timeout=60 Never Fired on a Stream With Keep-Alives</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://dev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/articles/3otvb2z646ytpt1hl2rv.jpg" alt="OpenAI timeout=60 Never Fired on a Stream With Keep-Alives" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Posted on Nov 14 • Originally published at Medium</p> <p>The openai Python SDK's timeout=60 limits each socket read, not the request, so a streamed completion that receives an SSE keep-alive comment every 15 seconds never times out, even though your loop never sees an event. Put a wall clock around the whole attempt instead: with AsyncOpenAI, asyncio.timeout(30) ended the same stalled stream at 30.0 to 30.1 seconds in every run.</p> <p>This story was written with the assistance of an AI writing program. The numbers come from openai 2.43.0 and httpx 0.28.1 on Python 3.14.4, run against a local fake OpenAI-compatible endpoint over plain HTTP and TLS. I did not test OpenAI's own API, and I do not know whether it sends comment lines.</p> <p>The fake endpoint answers POST /v1/chat/completions with text/event-stream, sends one normal data: chunk containing "Hello", and then stops producing tokens. In the silent variant it sends nothing more and holds the connection open. In the heartbeat variant it writes : keep-alive every 15 seconds and never sends [DONE].</p> <p>The client copies the settings of a real pipeline I reviewed this week: OpenAI(timeout=60.0, max_retries=0), stream=True, and a for chunk in stream loop. Each scenario ran as its own process under a 150-second timeout command, so exit code 124 means it was still blocked when the cap hit.</p> <p>Result lines from one plain-HTTP run, all scenarios in parallel:</p> <p>The silent stream failed at 60.4 to 60.6 seconds across three runs, as expected. The heartbeat stream was still waiting at 150 seconds in all three, including the TLS run. Nothing in the loop body ran after the first chunk.</p> <p>Look at the type in the silent case: httpx.ReadTimeout, not openai.APITimeoutError. The SDK converts timeouts into its own exception while it sends the request; once you are iterating, the raw httpx exception comes through. An except openai.APITimeoutError around a stream misses it.</p> <p>Two pieces combine. First, the SDK's SSE decoder discards comment lines: openai/_streaming.py has if line.startswith(":"): return None, which is correct for the format, so your code never learns that bytes arrived. Second, timeout=60 becomes httpx.Timeout(60), which sets the same 60 seconds for connect, read, write and pool acquisition. None of the four is a total. The read limit restarts on every successful read, and each comment is one.</p> <p>So the 60 seconds measure silence on the socket, not progress on your completion. A heartbeat every 15 seconds means the socket is never silent for 60.</p> <p>I hit the same shape with requests last week, when a server dripping one byte every three seconds kept timeout=5 busy for 57 seconds. The difference here is that the bytes are invisible: no partial content, no log line, nothing that tells you the call is still alive.</p> <p>This is not exotic. The HTML Standard's section on server-sent events suggests sending a comment line every 15 seconds or so, because some legacy proxies drop connections that go quiet. OpenRouter's streaming docs say it occasionally sends comments such as : OPENROUTER PROCESSING to prevent connection timeouts. Any gateway, proxy or self-hosted server that follows that advice turns a per-read timeout into no timeout while the model is stuck.</p> <p>With AsyncOpenAI, I put asyncio.timeout around the request and the iteration together. This is the exact function I ran this morning, pointed at the fake endpoint through OPENAI_BASE_URL:</p> <p>It raised TimeoutError at 30.0 seconds in both runs this morning; an earlier version of the test ended at 30.0 to 30.1 seconds in three runs. I also checked the socket. Right after the timeout, ss showed no established connection from the client, and the server's next keep-alive write, at 45 seconds, failed with BrokenPipeError. Wrapping the loop in async with stream: made no difference in the same two runs; the cancellation had already closed the connection.</p> <p>Sync code has no cancellation, so I tried a threading.Timer that fires at 30 seconds. Calling stream.close() from the timer did not interrupt the blocked read. The loop only failed when the next keep-alive arrived, with httpx.ReadError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor at 45.4 to 45.5 seconds. So a 30-second deadline ended at 45 seconds. I did not test close() against a silent stream.</p> <p>Shutting down the socket worked. The timer took the raw socket from stream.response.extensions["network_stream"].get_extra_info("socket") and called shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR), and the loop ended at 30.4 to 30.5 seconds over plain HTTP and TLS. That reaches into a low-level httpx response extension, so I would rather move the call into async code or a worker process that can be killed.</p> <p>If you run a gateway in front of a model API, does it send comment lines while the model thinks?</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails. DEV Community © 2016 - 2026.</p> <p>We're a place where coders share, stay up-to-date and grow their careers.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://dev.to/acemeridian/openai-timeout60-never-fired-on-a-stream-with-keep-alives-10o7" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9696"> <h2>#9696. LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://cdn-uploads.huggingface.co/production/uploads/6484ca4d5ff9a3d2ee52a83b/6KFZDHIJkxpICiErHLqAw.gif" alt="LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>LLMs rely on their context to generate the next set of tokens. Over a long trajectory, the context fills with numerous types of components: a system prompt, past conversation turns, instructions that act on retrieved documents, tool responses or user data, requirements constraining the allowed output, and reasoning chains. The context carries a rich structure, most of which is either implicit to the model or encoded in formats such as JSON that were not designed to be digested by LLMs. This is one of the main reasons LLMs, particularly those on the smaller end of the scale, are brittle and sometimes fail in unexpected ways. The lack of explicit structure can also be exploited by attackers, for example, in the form of prompt injections.</p> <p>To address this, we developed LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced “lemon”), an LLM-native markup language for explicitly communicating structure and semantics to the models. Semantically coherent components are marked with meaningful tags which are wrapped in reserved special-token delimiters. Data schemas, including nesting, are stated in a way that is unambiguous to a causal LLM. Unique IDs make it possible to point to specific instructions, which could reside anywhere in the context, and bind them to the data payloads they should act on, analogous to the way functions are called and arguments are passed to them in programming languages.</p> <p>Today we are releasing two experimental preview models, derived from Granite 4.1 base models, trained to consume and generate LLMON-marked text: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview. We are also releasing a GitHub repo, which includes a toolkit for working with LLMON and examples of workflows and templates.</p> <p>JSON was designed for parsers, not for causal language models. The tokenizer is not constrained to respect the grammar, and structure is encoded by tokens ({, ", :) that may also appear in normal text. To a model, a quotation mark inside a document and a quotation mark that closes a field are the same token. Escaping rules that are clear to a parser are only statistical patterns to a model. Nesting depth is encoded by counting brackets, which transformers are known to be weak at, especially over long spans.</p> <p>LLMON, on the other hand, is an XML-like markup whose structural delimiters are reserved special tokens rather than characters, so structure and content use separate parts of the vocabulary. Tags are stated at the beginning of each span, and the boundaries between spans are explicit. Nested structures are stated locally so the model does not need to keep track of the hierarchy over long spans.</p> <p>Since most teams already have pipelines built around JSON, we created conversion tools and example notebooks that translate JSON to LLMON and back in a lossless manner.</p> <p>LLMON does not replace chat templates; rather, it enriches them. Where regular chat templates tell the model which part belongs to which role (system, user, assistant), LLMON tells it what each component means and how components relate to each other, within and across roles.</p> <p>The LLMON preview models ship with their own chat template, so you build the same messages list you would pass to any chat model and call apply_chat_template as usual; it renders the LLMON shown below. The only difference is that a turn can now name its parts and mark each one exec: True or False. A part marked True is bound into the exec block at the bottom of the rendered output, which states which instruction to run and what it operates on; a part marked False is still rendered into the context but is referenced by nothing.</p> <p>Which the model receives as the following (with newlines and indentation added here for readability, as the template emits none):</p> <p>The two-character block IDs are drawn from a fixed set that this tokenizer encodes as single tokens, so addressing a block always costs two tokens regardless of which ID is drawn.</p> <p>The role is still a single user turn, but its components reach the model as five separate addressable blocks, bound together by a sixth (the exec block) that states: run this instruction, on this data, subject to these two requirements, and put the answer in the block named here, which is the same assistant block the model then fills. A conventional template would have flattened all components into one string and left the model to infer which part was the task, which was the subject, and which were constraints.</p> <p>Indirect prompt injection is a type of attack where a malicious instruction is hidden in a data payload, such as a retrieved document, a tool response, or user-provided data. This is the problem LLMON’s instruction/data separation is designed to address.</p> <p>We compared the LLMON previews against several open-source and closed-source models. We evaluated on the OPI benchmark, which places the injection in the data of classic NLP tasks. Several attack strategies are employed. We report robustness, defined as 1 − attack success rate: the share of attacks where the model does not carry out the injected instruction.</p> <p>All non-LLMON models are highly susceptible, carrying out the injected instructions with high probability. LLMON practically eliminates the problem on this benchmark, avoiding 47% more attacks relative to the best frontier model that we tested, and 95% more than the best open-source model. We observe similar trends on other benchmarks (ASB and StruQ). It is worth noting that these benchmarks test robustness to static indirect prompt injections. The instruction/data separation directly addresses this type of attack. We are actively working on also improving adaptive attacks which unfold over many chat turns.</p> <p>Safety gains don’t come at the expense of general capability. Across standard benchmark categories, the LLMON models perform on par with the Granite 4.1 Instruct models.</p> <p>In short, if you’re experimenting with Granite 4.1 3B or 8B today, you can swap in the LLMON preview and should see comparable general performance with much stronger resistance to prompt injection. No conversion pipeline is required. Naming the turn's parts (e.g., instruction, data, requirement as in the example above) is enough. The shipped chat template turns those into LLMON blocks for you. Our LLMON-converters library goes one level deeper: if a part is itself structured, such as a JSON document, LLMONizing it preserves that structure as typed, individually addressable blocks, instead of one opaque string.</p> <p>The models start from Granite 4.1 base checkpoints rather than the released instruct models, so LLMON behavior is learned during post-training rather than layered on an existing chat format.</p> <p>LLMON defines six delimiters that mark the start and end of tags and allow nesting and anchoring; they are installed in the tokenizer as reserved single tokens. We re-serialized a conventional instruction-tuning corpus into LLMON: every prompt component becomes its own addressable block, and each turn carries an execution block naming which instruction to run, which inputs it operates on, and where the output goes. The task mix is the one a normal instruct model sees (chat, multi-turn, RAG, tool calling), which is why benchmark performance stays close to the conventionally tuned model. In addition, we augment the data with decoy instructions and data blocks that are present in context but deliberately left unbound, while the target output is unchanged. So the model learns to follow the dependencies dictated by the execution block and ignore the rest. Reinforcement learning follows: five sequential GRPO stages spanning multi-domain reasoning, RLHF, knowledge calibration, and math, followed by a final DPO stage on a thousand on-policy preference pairs built from the model’s own responses to injection attempts.</p> <p>The resulting privilege rule falls out of this layout rather than an added guardrail: an instruction reached through an execution block is authoritative, while anything reached as input (data, documents, tool schemas, tool results) is material to read, not a command to follow. Furthermore, instructions and data spans that are not called on in the execution block are ignored. This is a learned behavior, not an enforced guarantee. To see how this plays out in the attention layers of a LLMON model, try the LLMON Attention Visualization on Hugging Face Spaces.</p> <p>LLMON is not tied to a fixed schema: you can choose tag names and structure that fit your domain and fine-tune an adapter to read and write them. We demonstrate this on ScienceWorld, a text-based benchmark where an agent carries out elementary science tasks (such as boiling water) by issuing one command at a time and receiving a score from the simulator. We defined a vocabulary capturing the structure in the planning trajectories involved in solving these tasks. The vocabulary includes tags such as instr.task.goal, req.planning_policy.rule, data.state.room, data.state.inventory and assistant.next_action. We rendered every step of ScienceWorld's reference solutions with these tags and tuned a LoRA on top of a LLMON model. The trained model then plays held-out games and writes its next action in the new vocabulary. This notebook walks through the full workflow, from converting reference trajectories to playing the test games and scoring the adapter against the untrained base model. Another example for tool-calling agents can be found in this notebook.</p> <p>This is an experimental preview, ready for exploration and evaluation but not for production.</p> <p>Tell us what you find: what worked, what broke, and which use cases you’d like to see. Post it in GitHub Discussions.</p> <p>Explore live Granite LLMON instruction attention</p> <p>That's really awesome! With an Apple pkl community renderer, you could potentially write PKL and render LLMON. 🥒🍋</p> <p>Any-to-pkl-community will convert json, yaml, toml to pkl, so just need the render part.</p> <p>Explore live Granite LLMON instruction attention</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/blog/ibm-granite/llmon-an-llm-native-markup-language-now-in-granite" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9695"> <h2>#9695. Mobile Manipulator Foundations and System Architecture — Ch.12: Standards and Regulations [EN]</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://dev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/articles/3otvb2z646ytpt1hl2rv.jpg" alt="Mobile Manipulator Foundations and System Architecture — Ch.12: Standards and Regulations [EN]" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>STATERA Library · Series 03 · Volume 01 · Chapter 12 · EN Source: https://github.com/Statera-Library/03_Vol_01_Mobile_Manipulator_Foundations_and_System_Architecture/blob/main/Chapter_12_Standards_and_Regulations/Chapter_12_Standards_and_Regulations_EN.md</p> <p>Volume 01. Mobile Manipulator Foundations and System Architecture</p> <p>Robot safety standards establish the technical principles and engineering requirements necessary to protect people, equipment, and surrounding environments during robotic operations. For mobile manipulators, safety extends beyond conventional industrial robot protection because autonomous navigation and articulated manipulation occur within the same operating system. Compliance therefore requires coordinated consideration of mobility, mechanical motion, control reliability, and human interaction.</p> <p>A mobile manipulator combines an autonomous mobile robot with a robotic arm, creating hazards that may occur independently or simultaneously. The mobile platform can collide with obstacles or pedestrians, while the manipulator may introduce crushing, trapping, impact, and unexpected movement risks. Safety engineering must address these combined hazards through systematic risk assessment, protective measures, and verification procedures covering the complete operational lifecycle.</p> <p>International safety standards provide a common foundation for designing and evaluating robotic systems. ISO 12100 establishes general machinery risk assessment and risk reduction principles, while ISO 10218 addresses industrial robot and robot system safety. ISO 3691-4 covers driverless industrial trucks and their systems, including relevant autonomous mobile platforms. Their applicability depends on the robot\'s intended use, configuration, and operating environment.</p> <p>Robot safety requirements begin with defining the intended application and foreseeable operating conditions. Engineers must identify whether the system operates inside factories, warehouses, hospitals, or public facilities, because each environment introduces different exposure scenarios.
