An integration layer coordinates both systems through defined communication interfaces. Depending on the equipment configuration, industrial protocols, application programming interfaces, and robotics middleware may be used to exchange commands and status information.</p> <p>Robot Operating System 2, or ROS 2, can provide a software framework for developing integrated mobile manipulation applications when supported by the selected components. Navigation software can coordinate mobile movement, while manipulation planning tools such as MoveIt 2 can support arm trajectory generation. However, compatibility depends on available drivers, interfaces, and vendor support. ROS 2 integration should therefore be treated as an engineering option rather than an inherent capability of every MiR configuration.</p> <p>The manipulation subsystem may use collaborative robotic arms when the application requires compact integration and operation near human workers. Collaborative robots provide capabilities such as force monitoring and configurable safety functions, but these features do not automatically make the complete mobile manipulation system safe. The combined robot must undergo application-specific risk assessment. Safety performance depends on the mobile base, manipulator, tooling, payload, operating speed, and surrounding environment.</p> <p>End-effector selection strongly influences the range of tasks supported by a MiR-based mobile manipulator. Parallel grippers can handle components with suitable contact surfaces, while vacuum grippers may be appropriate for boxes or flat objects. Specialized tools can support machine tending, inspection, and assembly operations. Each end effector introduces requirements involving gripping force, electrical power, pneumatic supply, sensing, and mechanical compatibility.</p> <p>Machine tending is a representative application in which a mobile manipulator delivers raw materials to manufacturing equipment and removes completed parts. The robot may approach a CNC machine, verify its position, and coordinate with the machine controller before opening access to the workspace. The manipulator then transfers parts between storage fixtures and the machine. Reliable execution requires synchronized communication, accurate positioning, and appropriate safety interlocks.</p> <p>Another application involves material transfer between production workstations. A mobile manipulator can collect parts from trays, bins, or designated fixtures and place them into receiving locations. This capability is useful when production equipment is distributed across a facility and direct conveyor connections are impractical. The robot may support multiple workstations, although task scheduling must account for travel time, manipulation duration, and equipment availability.</p> <p>The integration of mobile manipulation with manufacturing execution systems enables automated coordination of production activities. A supervisory system can assign tasks according to material demand, workstation status, and operational priorities. Completion messages and exception reports allow the manufacturing system to maintain visibility into robotic operations. Effective integration requires consistent identification of materials, reliable communication, and clearly defined responsibility for task execution.</p> <p>Fleet management becomes increasingly important when multiple MiR platforms operate within the same facility. Centralized coordination can distribute transportation requests, manage traffic, and reduce unnecessary movement. Mobile manipulators introduce additional scheduling constraints because each task includes both navigation and physical handling. Fleet-level optimization must therefore consider robot availability, arm capabilities, workstation accessibility, battery state, and expected task duration.</p> <p>Energy management is another significant engineering consideration. The mobile platform supplies energy for driving, navigation sensors, computing equipment, and onboard control systems. An integrated robotic arm may require additional electrical power during acceleration, lifting, and gripping operations. Engineers must determine whether the arm uses the platform\'s power system or a separate supply. Battery sizing and charging strategies should reflect the complete operating duty cycle.</p> <p>System reliability depends on the successful coordination of several independently complex subsystems. Navigation failures, communication interruptions, positioning errors, and unsuccessful grasps can prevent task completion. A supervisory controller should detect abnormal conditions and execute appropriate recovery procedures. These may include repeating localization, retrying a grasp, returning to a safe position, or requesting operator assistance when automated recovery is not possible.</p> <p>Safety architecture must address hazards arising from both mobile movement and robotic manipulation. A mobile base may encounter pedestrians or vehicles, while the robotic arm introduces risks associated with joint motion, gripping forces, and falling objects. Safety functions must consider the complete operating envelope and interactions between subsystems. Applicable requirements may include ISO 3691-4 for driverless industrial trucks and relevant industrial robot safety standards, depending on system classification.</p> <p>Performance evaluation should consider the complete task cycle rather than isolated navigation or manipulation results. Important measurements include travel time, docking accuracy, grasp success rate, placement repeatability, task completion rate, and operational availability. System throughput depends on how efficiently these activities are coordinated. A high-performance manipulator cannot compensate for excessive travel delays, and accurate navigation cannot overcome unreliable object handling.</p> <p>The economic benefits of MiR-based mobile manipulation arise from the possibility of sharing robotic resources across multiple workstations. Instead of installing a dedicated manipulator at every location, one mobile system may perform tasks at several machines. This can improve equipment utilization in suitable applications. However, travel time, docking requirements, integration complexity, and production scheduling may reduce the expected benefits, making detailed workflow analysis essential.</p> <p>Compared with fixed industrial automation, mobile manipulation provides greater flexibility but introduces additional uncertainty. Fixed robots operate within carefully calibrated workspaces, while mobile systems must repeatedly establish their position relative to external equipment. This creates additional requirements for localization, calibration, mechanical stability, and error recovery. The engineering challenge is to maintain acceptable manipulation performance despite the variability introduced by mobility.</p> <p>MiR-based mobile manipulators also illustrate the distinction between modular integration and fully unified robotic architecture. Combining commercially available components can reduce initial development effort, but the integrator remains responsible for mechanical compatibility, electrical interfaces, communication reliability, and system-level safety. Successful integration requires careful validation of interactions between components rather than assuming that individually reliable subsystems will automatically produce a reliable complete system.</p> <p>From a product strategy perspective, modular mobile manipulation offers opportunities for manufacturers seeking adaptable automation without extensive facility reconstruction. Applications with moderate handling loads, repeatable object geometries, and distributed workstations are particularly relevant. However, not every industrial process benefits from mobility. High-speed repetitive operations at a single location may remain better suited to fixed robotic cells with dedicated material-handling infrastructure.</p> <p>The broader significance of integrating MiR platforms with robotic arms lies in demonstrating how autonomous transportation can evolve into physical task execution. The mobile base extends the manipulator\'s operational reach across the facility, while the robotic arm enables direct interaction with materials and equipment. For engineers developing industrial mobile manipulators, this case emphasizes modular architecture, precise docking, coordinated control, functional safety, and system-level validation as essential foundations for reliable deployment.</p> <p>The OTTO-Motoman concept represents an industrial mobile manipulation architecture that combines an OTTO autonomous mobile robot with a Yaskawa Motoman robotic arm. This configuration integrates autonomous material transportation with robotic handling capabilities. Rather than relying exclusively on fixed automation stations, the system can potentially move between production locations and perform loading, unloading, and material transfer operations through coordinated mobility and manipulation.</p> <p>OTTO Motors develops autonomous mobile robots designed for industrial material transportation, while Yaskawa Motoman provides robotic manipulators for manufacturing automation. Combining these technologies creates a modular engineering approach in which the mobile platform and manipulator retain distinct functional responsibilities. The resulting system should be understood as an integration architecture rather than a single standardized product with universally defined specifications.</p> <p>The primary objective of an OTTO-Motoman integration is to extend robotic manipulation beyond fixed workstations. A mobile manipulator can transport components between production areas and interact directly with machines, fixtures, and material containers. This approach is particularly relevant to manufacturing facilities where equipment is distributed across multiple locations. Its practical value depends on balancing transportation flexibility with manipulation accuracy, operational reliability, and integration complexity.</p> <p>The mechanical architecture consists of a mobile platform, robotic arm, mounting structure, and application-specific end effector. The platform must support the combined weight of the manipulator, controller, tooling, and transported payload. Engineers must evaluate structural stiffness, mounting strength, and center-of-gravity movement during arm operation. Excessive arm extension or unfavorable payload positioning can introduce tipping moments and compromise system stability.</p> <p>Payload selection requires independent evaluation of the mobile platform and robotic arm. The mobile robot\'s rated capacity must accommodate all installed equipment and transported materials, while the manipulator\'s payload rating must include the gripper and handled object. Dynamic forces generated during acceleration, braking, and arm movement introduce additional loading conditions. Consequently, nominal payload ratings alone are insufficient for determining the safe operating envelope.</p> <p>The OTTO mobile platform provides navigation and material transportation functions within mapped industrial environments. Localization, obstacle detection, and route planning allow the robot to move between designated workstations. Navigation performance depends on environmental geometry, floor conditions, traffic density, and operational constraints. The platform must also approach manipulation locations consistently enough to support subsequent alignment and positioning procedures.</p> <p>The Motoman robotic arm provides controlled manipulation through coordinated joint movement and end-effector operation. Depending on the selected model, the manipulator may support machine tending, component transfer, inspection, or assembly-related handling. Its working envelope must be evaluated relative to the mobile platform and surrounding equipment. Joint limits, reachability, collision constraints, and payload-dependent performance determine which tasks can be executed reliably.</p> <p>Precise docking is a critical requirement because autonomous navigation accuracy may not satisfy the tolerances of industrial manipulation. The mobile platform must establish a repeatable position relative to the target machine or fixture. Mechanical docking features, fiducial markers, and vision-based alignment can provide additional positioning accuracy. The appropriate method depends on the required repeatability, workstation geometry, and environmental variability.</p> <p>A typical operating cycle begins when a supervisory system assigns a transportation and manipulation task. The mobile robot navigates to the source workstation and confirms its arrival. After establishing the required alignment, the robotic arm retrieves the target component and places it in a secure transport position. The platform then travels to the destination, where the manipulator performs the corresponding unloading or placement operation.</p> <p>Coordination between navigation and manipulation requires a clearly defined operational state machine. The system must distinguish traveling, docking, manipulation, recovery, and emergency conditions. During transportation, the robotic arm should remain in a configuration that preserves stability and avoids collisions. Manipulation generally begins after the mobile platform reaches a verified operating position, simplifying control and reducing uncertainty associated with simultaneous movement.</p> <p>The control architecture typically includes separate controllers for the autonomous mobile robot and Motoman manipulator. The mobile controller manages navigation and platform motion, while the robot controller executes joint trajectories and end-effector commands. An integration controller coordinates task execution through communication interfaces and status signals. Successful operation depends on deterministic state transitions, reliable command acknowledgment, and consistent fault handling.</p> <p>Industrial communication may involve Ethernet-based interfaces, programmable logic controllers, digital input and output signals, or application-specific protocols. The selected architecture must support task commands, position confirmation, machine readiness, and safety-related coordination. Communication delays or inconsistent status information can interrupt the handling sequence. Engineers should therefore define explicit interface control specifications and validate communication behavior under abnormal operating conditions.</p> <p>Machine tending provides a representative application for the OTTO-Motoman architecture. The mobile manipulator can deliver raw components to manufacturing equipment and remove completed parts after processing. Interaction with CNC machines requires coordination with machine doors, fixtures, and operating states. Accurate placement and reliable interlocks are essential because positioning errors can damage components or interfere with automated machining operations.</p> <p>Material handling between assembly stations represents another potential application. A mobile manipulator can collect components from standardized trays and distribute them to multiple workstations. This approach may reduce the need for dedicated conveyors or fixed robotic cells at every location. However, task efficiency depends on transportation distance, manipulation time, workstation availability, and the number of operations completed during each visit.</p> <p>End-effector design strongly influences system versatility. Parallel grippers can handle rigid mechanical components, while vacuum grippers may be suitable for flat surfaces or packaged materials. Specialized tooling can support machine loading, inspection, and component positioning. Each configuration introduces requirements for electrical power, pneumatic supply, gripping force, sensing, and tool communication. End-effector selection must therefore reflect both object characteristics and operational constraints.</p> <p>Power architecture requires careful evaluation because the mobile platform and robotic arm may have different electrical requirements. The manipulator controller can demand substantial power during acceleration and lifting, while the mobile base continuously supplies navigation, sensing, and computing functions. Integration may require dedicated power conversion, auxiliary batteries, or external power connections. Energy storage and charging strategies must support the intended operating cycle.</p> <p>Safety engineering must consider hazards introduced by combining a moving industrial platform with an articulated robotic arm. Mobile navigation creates collision risks involving personnel and equipment, while manipulation introduces hazards associated with joint motion, gripping forces, and falling objects. Safety functions must cover the combined operating envelope. Applicable standards and protective measures depend on the final system configuration and its intended industrial environment.</p> <p>Functional safety integration requires coordination between the mobile platform\'s protective functions and the manipulator\'s safety controller. Emergency stop behavior, protective stopping, restart conditions, and safe operating states must be defined at the system level. A safety event affecting one subsystem may require coordinated action by the other. Independent component certifications do not automatically establish compliance for the complete integrated machine.</p> <p>System reliability depends on the interaction of navigation, docking, manipulation, communication, and supervisory control. A failure in any subsystem can interrupt the entire task cycle. Recovery strategies may include repeated localization, docking retries, manipulation reattempts, or controlled return to a safe state. Fault information should be recorded to support diagnostics, maintenance planning, and continuous operational improvement.</p> <p>Performance evaluation should measure complete task execution rather than isolated robot capabilities. Relevant indicators include navigation time, docking repeatability, manipulation cycle time, grasp success rate, task completion rate, and operational availability. System throughput depends on how efficiently transportation and handling activities are coordinated. Long travel distances or repeated alignment failures can significantly reduce productivity despite a high-performance robotic arm.</p> <p>Fleet management becomes important when multiple mobile manipulators share production areas. Centralized coordination can allocate tasks, manage traffic, and schedule charging operations. Unlike transportation-only AMRs, mobile manipulators occupy workstations while performing physical handling operations. Fleet scheduling must therefore consider manipulation duration, equipment availability, and workstation access restrictions in addition to navigation requirements.</p> <p>The economic justification for OTTO-Motoman integration depends on the ability to distribute robotic manipulation across multiple manufacturing locations. A single mobile system may replace selected repetitive handling activities performed at several stations. However, additional integration costs, docking infrastructure, maintenance requirements, and operational delays must be included in the analysis. Return on investment should reflect realistic utilization and the total cost of ownership.</p> <p>Compared with fixed industrial robots, the OTTO-Motoman architecture offers greater deployment flexibility but introduces additional engineering complexity. Fixed manipulators operate within stable, calibrated workspaces, whereas mobile systems must repeatedly establish accurate spatial relationships with external equipment. This creates additional requirements for localization, mechanical stability, calibration, and error recovery. The resulting design must balance flexibility against precision and operational efficiency.</p> <p>The broader significance of the OTTO-Motoman case lies in demonstrating how industrial autonomous mobility and robotic manipulation can be combined through modular system integration. Its engineering value is not limited to a particular mobile platform or manipulator model. The architecture emphasizes mechanical compatibility, precise docking, coordinated control, functional safety, and reliable communication as foundations for practical industrial mobile manipulation systems.</p> <p>A warehouse picking system based on mobile manipulation combines autonomous navigation, object recognition, robotic grasping, and inventory coordination to retrieve products from storage locations. Unlike transportation-only autonomous mobile robots, these systems interact directly with individual items. Their objective is to automate repetitive order fulfillment activities while maintaining picking accuracy, operational flexibility, and compatibility with existing warehouse infrastructure.</p> <p>Warehouse picking operations involve identifying requested products, locating their storage positions, retrieving items, and transferring them to designated containers or processing stations. Mobile manipulators can execute these activities across distributed shelving areas without requiring a fixed robotic arm at every location. This architecture is particularly useful in warehouses handling diverse products, changing inventory distributions, and variable order volumes.</p> <p>The mechanical architecture typically includes an autonomous mobile base, robotic arm, end effector, perception sensors, and onboard storage. The mobile platform provides transportation between storage locations, while the manipulator reaches into shelves or containers. Engineers must consider payload capacity, manipulator reach, center-of-gravity movement, and available aisle clearance. These constraints determine which storage configurations and product categories can be supported.</p> <p>Perception is essential because warehouse items vary in geometry, packaging, orientation, and visibility. RGB cameras, depth sensors, and three-dimensional perception algorithms can identify objects and estimate their positions. The system must distinguish target products from neighboring inventory while accounting for occlusion and inconsistent lighting. Reliable perception provides the spatial information required for grasp planning and collision-free manipulation.</p> <p>Object recognition may rely on barcode identification, visual classification, instance segmentation, or combinations of these methods. Barcode scanning provides reliable identification when labels are visible, while visual recognition supports products with partially obscured markings. Instance segmentation separates individual objects within crowded storage areas. The appropriate approach depends on inventory characteristics, labeling practices, and the accuracy required by warehouse operations.</p> <p>Grasp planning translates perception results into executable manipulation actions. The robot must determine suitable contact points, approach directions, and end-effector configurations. Parallel grippers are appropriate for many rigid objects, while vacuum grippers can handle compatible packages with accessible surfaces. Grasp selection must account for object weight, surface properties, center of mass, and surrounding obstacles to reduce failed retrieval attempts.</p> <p>Mobile navigation enables the robot to travel between storage locations while avoiding workers, vehicles, and temporary obstacles. Localization and mapping establish the robot\'s position within the warehouse. However, navigation accuracy alone may not satisfy manipulation requirements. Additional shelf-relative localization, fiducial markers, or vision-based alignment may be necessary to achieve repeatable positioning before the robotic arm begins its task.</p> <p>A typical picking cycle begins when a warehouse management system assigns an order or retrieval task. The robot identifies the required storage location and navigates toward the corresponding shelf. After confirming its position, the perception system locates the target item and generates a grasp candidate. The manipulator retrieves the object, verifies successful acquisition, and transfers it into an onboard container or designated receiving area.</p> <p>Picking verification is necessary to maintain inventory accuracy and prevent incorrect order fulfillment. The system may combine visual confirmation, barcode scanning, gripper feedback, and weight measurements to verify the retrieved product. Verification results are communicated to the warehouse management system, allowing inventory records to remain synchronized. Failed verification should trigger recovery procedures rather than silently recording an unsuccessful operation as completed.</p> <p>Task planning determines the order in which products are collected and how mobile resources are allocated. Batch picking allows multiple order lines to be retrieved during a single warehouse route, reducing unnecessary travel. Route optimization must consider shelf locations, robot payload capacity, container availability, and order priorities. Effective scheduling balances transportation efficiency against manipulation time and operational deadlines.</p> <p>Warehouse management system integration connects physical robot operations with digital inventory and order information. The integration layer receives task assignments, reports completion status, and communicates exceptions. Accurate product identifiers and storage coordinates are essential for consistent execution. Communication interfaces must also handle temporary network interruptions, duplicate commands, and inventory changes without creating inconsistent transaction records.</p> <p>The software architecture commonly separates navigation, perception, manipulation planning, task execution, and supervisory control. Each subsystem performs specialized functions while exchanging information through defined interfaces. A supervisory state machine coordinates movement, docking, grasping, verification, and recovery. This separation supports modular development but requires careful synchronization to prevent conflicting commands or unsafe transitions between operating states.</p> <p>Error recovery is a critical requirement because warehouse environments contain irregular packaging, crowded shelves, and unexpected object arrangements. A grasp may fail because of inaccurate localization, insufficient clearance, or unstable contact. The robot should detect unsuccessful retrieval and determine whether repositioning, repeated perception, or an alternative grasp is appropriate. Persistent failures may require human assistance or reassignment of the task.</p> <p>Safety engineering must address hazards associated with mobile movement and robotic manipulation. The platform may encounter pedestrians and material-handling vehicles, while the arm can introduce collision, pinching, and dropped-object risks. Protective functions must account for the combined operating envelope and changing robot configurations. Risk assessment should consider normal operation, maintenance, manual intervention, and foreseeable abnormal conditions.</p> <p>Performance evaluation should measure the complete picking workflow rather than isolated component capabilities. Relevant indicators include item recognition accuracy, grasp success rate, picking cycle time, travel distance, task completion rate, and intervention frequency. Effective throughput depends on both manipulation reliability and transportation efficiency. System availability and recovery time are particularly important when robots operate continuously across multiple shifts.</p> <p>Energy management influences the operational capacity of warehouse picking robots. Driving, sensing, onboard computing, arm movement, and gripping mechanisms consume electrical power throughout the task cycle. Battery capacity and charging schedules must support expected workloads without excessive downtime. Energy-aware scheduling can coordinate charging with periods of lower demand, improving robot availability and reducing interruptions to order fulfillment.</p> <p>Fleet coordination becomes important when multiple mobile manipulators share storage aisles and processing stations. A fleet management system can allocate picking tasks, manage traffic, and prevent congestion around frequently accessed shelves. Scheduling must account for robot capabilities, storage accessibility, battery levels, and task priorities. Effective coordination improves overall warehouse throughput rather than merely optimizing individual robot movements.</p> <p>Warehouse infrastructure strongly influences deployment feasibility. Shelf dimensions, aisle widths, floor conditions, lighting, and product placement practices determine whether robots can navigate and manipulate reliably. Standardized containers and predictable storage arrangements simplify perception and grasp planning. Although mobile manipulation can reduce dependence on fixed automation, successful deployment still requires compatibility between robotic capabilities and warehouse operating procedures.</p> <p>Economic evaluation must consider equipment acquisition, software integration, maintenance, charging infrastructure, and operational support. Potential benefits include reduced repetitive manual handling, improved inventory traceability, and flexible resource allocation. However, high product variability and frequent picking failures can reduce productivity gains. Return on investment should therefore be calculated using realistic task completion rates, utilization assumptions, and total ownership costs.</p> <p>The broader significance of warehouse picking systems lies in integrating autonomous mobility with direct physical interaction and digital logistics coordination. These systems demonstrate how mobile manipulators can extend warehouse automation beyond transportation into item-level operations. Their successful implementation depends on reliable perception, precise positioning, adaptable grasping, robust recovery, and coordinated system integration rather than any single robotic capability.</p> <p>Hospital logistics systems based on mobile manipulation combine autonomous navigation, robotic handling, and hospital information systems to transport and manage medical supplies. Unlike conventional delivery robots that move entire carts or containers, mobile manipulators can interact directly with individual items and storage interfaces. Their objective is to reduce repetitive transportation tasks while improving material availability, operational traceability, and workflow efficiency.</p> <p>Hospitals require continuous movement of medications, laboratory specimens, sterile instruments, linens, meals, and medical consumables between departments. These activities involve different handling requirements, delivery priorities, and environmental constraints. A mobile manipulation system can support selected logistics tasks by collecting, transporting, and depositing materials at designated locations, reducing the need for clinical personnel to perform routine transfers.</p> <p>The mechanical architecture typically integrates an autonomous mobile base, robotic arm, end effector, storage compartment, and perception sensors. The mobile platform provides transportation through hospital corridors, while the manipulator interacts with shelves, cabinets, trays, or receiving stations. Engineers must consider payload capacity, manipulator reach, platform dimensions, and stability. Compact construction is particularly important in crowded corridors and confined clinical spaces.</p> <p>Hospital navigation presents challenges because the operating environment contains patients, visitors, medical staff, wheelchairs, and mobile equipment. The robot must detect dynamic obstacles and adapt its motion without disrupting clinical activities. Localization and mapping support movement between departments, while obstacle avoidance maintains appropriate separation from surrounding objects. Navigation performance must remain reliable despite changing corridor conditions and temporary obstructions.</p> <p>Elevator integration is often necessary because hospital logistics operations span multiple floors. The robot may require communication with elevator controllers, automated doors, and building management systems. Successful integration involves requesting elevator service, entering safely, selecting the destination floor, and resuming navigation after arrival. These operations require reliable coordination because elevator congestion or communication failures can interrupt time-sensitive deliveries.</p> <p>The manipulation subsystem enables interaction with medical supply containers, storage racks, and transfer stations. Depending on the application, the robot may use parallel grippers, vacuum tools, or specialized handling mechanisms. Grasp planning must consider package geometry, object weight, and accessibility. Medical materials may require controlled handling to prevent damage, contamination, or unintended movement during retrieval and placement.</p> <p>Perception systems help identify objects, locate storage positions, and verify successful transfers. RGB cameras, depth sensors, barcode scanners, and identification technologies may be combined according to operational requirements. Visual recognition supports object localization, while barcode or RFID identification can improve item traceability. Accurate verification is particularly important when handling materials with strict inventory or delivery requirements.</p> <p>A typical logistics task begins when a hospital management application or supervisory system generates a transportation request. The robot identifies the collection point and navigates toward the corresponding department. After confirming its position, the manipulator retrieves the designated material and places it in a secure transport compartment. The robot then travels to the destination, verifies the receiving location, and completes the delivery operation.</p> <p>Secure transport is essential for medications, laboratory samples, and other sensitive materials. Lockable compartments, access authorization, and delivery confirmation can reduce unauthorized handling. Some applications may require temperature monitoring, environmental protection, or documented chain-of-custody procedures. These requirements depend on the transported material and applicable institutional policies. A mobile manipulator must therefore support application-specific security and traceability functions.</p> <p>Hospital information system integration connects robotic operations with clinical logistics workflows. Task assignments may originate from inventory management, pharmacy, laboratory, or facility management applications. The integration layer exchanges delivery requests, status updates, and completion records. Reliable communication helps maintain consistency between physical material movement and digital records, while access controls protect sensitive operational information.</p> <p>Task scheduling must account for delivery urgency, department locations, robot availability, and handling constraints. Routine supply replenishment can be scheduled in batches, while urgent requests may require immediate prioritization. Route planning should consider travel distance, elevator waiting time, restricted areas, and expected congestion. Effective scheduling balances operational efficiency with the service requirements of different hospital departments.</p> <p>Safety engineering is especially important because robots operate near vulnerable patients and busy clinical personnel. The mobile platform must manage collision risks, while the manipulator introduces potential hazards from joint movement, gripping forces, and dropped objects. Protective functions should cover both navigation and handling operations. Risk assessment must consider normal deliveries, unexpected human interaction, emergency situations, and manual intervention.</p> <p>Infection prevention introduces requirements beyond those found in ordinary warehouse logistics. External surfaces, storage compartments, and handling tools may need to support approved cleaning and disinfection procedures. Materials intended for sterile environments require appropriate separation and handling protocols. Robot design should minimize difficult-to-clean surfaces and avoid unnecessary contact with clinical equipment. Compliance depends on hospital infection-control policies and the intended application.</p> <p>Human-robot interaction is necessary because hospital personnel must understand robot status and respond to exceptional situations. Visual indicators, audible notifications, and user interfaces can communicate movement intentions, delivery progress, and fault conditions. Staff may need to authorize access, confirm receipt, or assist with failed transfers. Interaction design should remain simple enough for personnel who are not robotics specialists.</p> <p>Operational reliability depends on successful coordination of navigation, manipulation, communication, and building infrastructure. A robot may encounter blocked corridors, unavailable elevators, inaccessible storage locations, or unsuccessful grasps. Recovery strategies should include route replanning, repeated localization, task retries, and controlled escalation to human operators. Critical deliveries require clear procedures when autonomous completion is not possible.</p> <p>Fleet management becomes important when multiple hospital robots serve different departments. A centralized system can allocate tasks, coordinate traffic, monitor battery status, and distribute workloads. Fleet scheduling should account for elevator capacity, delivery deadlines, robot capabilities, and charging availability. Effective coordination reduces congestion and prevents several robots from competing for the same infrastructure resources.</p> <p>Energy management must support continuous hospital operations, including overnight and weekend activities. Battery capacity determines available operating time, while charging schedules influence robot availability. The mobile base, robotic arm, perception sensors, and computing equipment all contribute to power consumption. Automated charging can reduce manual intervention, but charging decisions must account for pending deliveries and operational priorities.</p> <p>Performance evaluation should consider delivery completion rate, transportation time, manipulation success rate, intervention frequency, and operational availability. Additional indicators may include elevator waiting time, delivery accuracy, and response time for urgent requests. Measuring complete workflows is more meaningful than evaluating navigation speed alone. Hospital logistics performance depends on reliable service delivery rather than maximum robot movement speed.</p> <p>Economic evaluation includes equipment acquisition, integration with hospital systems, building interface modifications, maintenance, and staff training. Potential benefits include reduced repetitive transport work, improved supply traceability, and more consistent logistics scheduling. However, deployment costs and operational complexity may offset expected savings. Return on investment should consider realistic utilization, labor allocation, service quality, and total ownership costs.</p> <p>The broader significance of hospital mobile manipulation lies in extending autonomous logistics beyond simple transportation. By combining navigation, object handling, secure delivery, and information system integration, these robots can support more complete material workflows. Successful deployment requires careful attention to safety, hygiene, reliability, human interaction, and institutional procedures. Hospital logistics therefore provides an important example of application-specific mobile manipulation in human-centered environments.</p> <p>Industrial mobile manipulators combine autonomous mobile platforms with robotic arms to perform physical operations across manufacturing environments. Unlike fixed industrial robots, these systems can relocate between workstations while maintaining manipulation capabilities. Their primary objective is to extend automation beyond stationary production cells, supporting flexible material handling, machine tending, inspection, and assembly operations within changing industrial layouts.</p> <p>The system architecture typically consists of a mobile base, robotic manipulator, end effector, perception sensors, onboard computing, and supervisory control software. Each subsystem contributes specialized capabilities that must operate as a coordinated whole. The mobile platform provides transportation and localization, while the manipulator performs physical interactions. Effective integration requires mechanical compatibility, reliable communication, synchronized control, and comprehensive safety engineering.</p> <p>Mechanical design begins with evaluating payload capacity, structural stiffness, center-of-gravity movement, and dynamic loading. The mobile platform must support the robotic arm, mounting structures, controllers, tooling, and transported materials. Arm extension and payload movement can introduce substantial overturning moments. Engineers must evaluate stability under acceleration, braking, turning, and manipulation conditions to establish a safe operating envelope.</p> <p>Manipulator selection depends on reach, payload, repeatability, degrees of freedom, and compatibility with industrial processes. Six-axis articulated arms provide flexibility for complex positioning tasks, while collaborative manipulators may support applications requiring operation near personnel. However, collaborative features do not automatically establish safety for the complete mobile system. The selected arm must satisfy application requirements without exceeding platform stability or power limitations.</p> <p>Autonomous navigation enables the robot to move between production stations while avoiding obstacles and adapting to environmental changes. Localization and mapping establish the platform\'s position within the facility. Industrial environments introduce challenges involving narrow aisles, moving equipment, reflective surfaces, and temporary obstructions. Reliable navigation requires suitable sensing, route planning, traffic coordination, and recovery procedures for unexpected conditions.</p> <p>Precision positioning is essential because navigation accuracy alone rarely satisfies industrial manipulation tolerances. A robot may reach a workstation while remaining misaligned with its fixtures or equipment. Docking mechanisms, fiducial markers, vision-based localization, and mechanical alignment features can improve positioning repeatability. High-precision applications may require additional calibration or external measurement systems to establish accurate relationships between the robot and workstation.</p> <p>Perception systems provide information about objects, workspaces, and environmental conditions. RGB cameras, depth sensors, industrial vision systems, and force sensors can support object detection, pose estimation, and contact monitoring. Sensor selection depends on required accuracy, lighting conditions, object geometry, and operating distance. Robust perception must account for occlusion, reflective materials, variable illumination, and changes in object placement.</p> <p>Manipulation planning converts task requirements and perception results into executable robot motions. The system must evaluate reachability, joint limits, collision constraints, and suitable grasp configurations. Motion planning algorithms generate trajectories that avoid surrounding equipment while maintaining required tool orientations. For contact-intensive operations, force feedback and compliant control may improve interaction reliability and reduce the risk of damaging components.</p> <p>A typical operating cycle begins when a supervisory controller receives a manufacturing task. The mobile platform navigates to the designated workstation and verifies its operating position. The manipulator then performs the required handling, inspection, or assembly operation. After completing the task, the robot confirms the result and either proceeds to another workstation or returns to a designated location for charging or standby.</p> <p>Coordinated control requires a supervisory state machine that manages navigation, docking, manipulation, verification, and recovery. In many applications, the mobile base remains stationary while the robotic arm operates. This reduces uncertainty and simplifies safety management. More advanced systems may coordinate simultaneous base and arm motion, but such operation introduces additional challenges involving dynamic stability, trajectory synchronization, and collision avoidance.</p> <p>Software integration commonly involves separate controllers for the mobile platform and robotic arm. Industrial communication protocols, application programming interfaces, and robotics middleware connect these subsystems. ROS 2 and manipulation planning frameworks may support integrated development when compatible drivers are available. Regardless of software architecture, reliable state synchronization, command acknowledgment, and fault handling are essential for continuous operation.</p> <p>Industrial mobile manipulators support machine tending by transporting materials to manufacturing equipment and transferring components between fixtures. Applications may include CNC loading, unloading, and automated part exchange. Successful implementation requires accurate docking, machine-controller communication, and safety interlocks. The robot must verify machine readiness before entering the working area and confirm successful part placement before processing resumes.</p> <p>Inspection applications use mobile manipulators to position cameras, scanners, or measurement probes at different locations. This approach can reduce the need for dedicated inspection equipment at every workstation. However, measurement accuracy depends on platform stability, manipulator calibration, sensor alignment, and environmental conditions. Precision inspection may require rigid docking, vibration control, and reference-based coordinate correction.</p> <p>Assembly applications involve component positioning, insertion, fastening, and other controlled interactions. These tasks often require higher precision and more sophisticated force control than simple material transportation. The robot must compensate for positioning uncertainty and mechanical tolerances. Successful assembly depends on coordinated perception, compliant manipulation, accurate tooling, and verification of the completed operation.</p> <p>Safety architecture must address hazards associated with both autonomous movement and robotic manipulation. Mobile platforms introduce collision risks, while robotic arms create additional hazards involving joint motion, gripping forces, and falling objects. Risk assessment must consider the complete operating envelope and foreseeable human interactions. Applicable standards and protective measures depend on system classification, intended application, and operating environment.</p> <p>Functional safety integration requires coordinated emergency stopping, protective stopping, safe speed control, and controlled restart procedures. Safety events affecting the mobile platform may require corresponding responses from the manipulator. The combined system must be validated as an integrated machine rather than relying solely on individual component certifications. Safety verification should include normal operations, abnormal conditions, maintenance activities, and recovery scenarios.</p> <p>Energy management is important because mobile manipulators supply power to propulsion, sensing, computing, robotic joints, and end effectors. Battery capacity and power conversion must support peak loads as well as average consumption. Charging strategies should reflect task duration, utilization, and operational priorities. Energy-aware scheduling can reduce unnecessary travel and coordinate charging with periods of lower production demand.</p> <p>Fleet management becomes necessary when multiple mobile manipulators operate across shared production areas. A centralized or distributed coordination system can allocate tasks, manage traffic, and schedule charging. Unlike transportation-only robots, mobile manipulators occupy workstations during physical operations. Effective scheduling must therefore account for manipulation duration, workstation availability, robot capabilities, and task dependencies.</p> <p>Reliability engineering focuses on maintaining successful operation across navigation, docking, perception, manipulation, and communication subsystems. Failures may arise from localization errors, unsuccessful grasps, unexpected obstacles, or equipment communication problems. Recovery strategies should include task retries, repositioning, recalibration, and controlled escalation to operators. Diagnostic logging supports maintenance planning and continuous performance improvement.</p> <p>Performance evaluation should measure complete task execution rather than isolated subsystem capabilities. Relevant indicators include navigation time, docking accuracy, manipulation success rate, cycle time, task completion rate, and operational availability. Overall throughput depends on transportation efficiency and manipulation reliability. A technically capable robot may still deliver limited productivity if travel delays, repeated alignment failures, or recovery interruptions dominate its operating cycle.</p> <p>Economic evaluation considers equipment investment, integration complexity, maintenance, facility modifications, and operational support. Mobile manipulation can improve resource utilization by allowing one robot to serve multiple workstations. However, additional travel time and positioning requirements may offset the benefits of flexibility. Return on investment should be assessed using realistic utilization, production throughput, labor allocation, and total ownership costs.</p> <p>The broader significance of industrial mobile manipulators lies in combining autonomous mobility with direct physical interaction across manufacturing environments. Their development represents a transition from isolated robotic workstations toward adaptable automation systems. Successful deployment depends on coordinated mechanical design, precise localization, reliable perception, robust manipulation, functional safety, and system-level validation that addresses the complete industrial workflow.</p> <p>Author: Richard Minsoo Go LinkedIn: Richard Minsoo Go</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails. DEV Community © 2016 - 2026.</p> <p>We're a place where coders share, stay up-to-date and grow their careers.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://dev.to/richard_minsoogo/mobile-manipulator-foundations-and-system-architecture-ch16-case-studies-en-44oc" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9680"> <h2>#9680. This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2025-07/Tarte-Tartin_2025_Lifestyle_ALT_H_1236.jpg" alt="This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>As fall baking season settles in, you're probably reaching for apples — and the many flavor-packed ingredients they produce. Applesauce cooks down into tangy apple butter to be cradled in a flaky galette, while a drop of boiled cider can deliver supercharged apple flavor to crumb cake. But the baking ingredient you may be overlooking may be something you associate more with salad dressings and wellness tonics: apple cider vinegar.</p> <p>This tangy, apple-y vinegar is a secret ingredient in some of our favorite fall recipes, including cookbook author Claire Saffitz’s Cinnamon-and-Sugar Apple Pie. While lemon juice is the standard acid used in most fruit pie fillings, Claire opts for apple cider vinegar here to complement the filling’s flavors. “It helps as a flavor enhancer, and I also like that it’s apple cider in an apple pie. It’s a nice symmetry,” she mentions.</p> <p>Similarly, apple cider vinegar is used in the cooking liquid alongside sugar and butter to caramelize apples in a Classic Apple Tarte Tatin. The benefit is twofold: Vinegar’s acidity helps cut the sweetness of the caramel, and it prevents the apples from getting too mushy, instead maintaining their fork-tender texture.</p> <p>Pastry chef and cookbook author Natasha Pickowicz often leans into the jolt vinegar can add, including adding a few drops to her cake soaks for an additional layer of flavor. “Cake soaks should have a balance of tart, sweet, and savory notes — just like vinaigrette for your favorite salad,” she writes in her cookbook More Than Cake. It can add intrigue to layered cakes like this Golden Spice Cake or Pumpkin Layer Cake. In her cookbook, she also calls for a glaze spiked with apple cider vinegar to brush onto an apple tart after baking. It’s the finishing touch “to further emphasize the tart’s resolute apple-ness,” she writes.</p> <p>Apple cider vinegar doesn’t need to be limited to only apple desserts, either. In our Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie, we call for apple cider vinegar as a foil to the brown sugar filling’s cloying sweetness. A spoonful of apple cider vinegar may not announce itself boldly, but it makes a small splash for brighter, more balanced bakes.</p> <p>For more fall baking inspiration, check out our Fall Flavor Edit.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>A grocery store shortcut for bakery-worthy treats.</p> <p>It's got cinnamon-scented apples, rich vanilla cake, and a sheer sweet glaze.</p> <p>Eschew classic crust and enter a diverse world of beloved fruit desserts.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/09/24/apple-cider-vinegar-recipes" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9679"> <h2>#9679. ProWritingAid VS Grammarly: Which Grammar Checker is Better in (2022) ?</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEjF7I9iAp1Tfc6kFmKNOYqqI2V1NjZ1ltfemNKGCo1nvQlCy0DWGe_hNag4uruW_SW6tMwc0M8sa4O7ca4zQ6Hiiu6TDi4VAohA3aTPmU4KuRqBC2KQpg3PB_55tjbwwO9ko2xAW-9QQdfpph0xVKiCDiMRKkrL8clOk90wa1arfXGW0VKIO182Qb31vw=s1920" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><img alt="Grammarly vs prowritingaid" border="0" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEjF7I9iAp1Tfc6kFmKNOYqqI2V1NjZ1ltfemNKGCo1nvQlCy0DWGe_hNag4uruW_SW6tMwc0M8sa4O7ca4zQ6Hiiu6TDi4VAohA3aTPmU4KuRqBC2KQpg3PB_55tjbwwO9ko2xAW-9QQdfpph0xVKiCDiMRKkrL8clOk90wa1arfXGW0VKIO182Qb31vw=w640-h360" title="Grammarly vs prowritingaid" width="640" /></a></div></h2><div style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b><span><a name="more"></a></span>ProWritingAid VS Grammarly:<span style="color: #3c4043;"><span style="background-color: white; font-size: 14px;"> </span></span></b></span><span style="color: #3c4043; font-family: Comfortaa;"><span style="font-size: 14px;"> When it comes to English grammar, there are two Big Players that everyone knows of: the Grammarly and ProWritingAid. but you are wondering which one to choose so here we write a detail article which will help you to choose the best one for you so Let's start</span></span></div><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">What is Grammarly?</span></h2><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Grammarly is a tool that checks for grammatical errors, spelling, and punctuation.it gives you comprehensive feedback on your writing. You can use this tool to proofread and edit articles, blog posts, emails, etc.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Grammarly also detects all types of mistakes, including sentence structure issues and misused words. It also gives you suggestions on style changes, punctuation, spelling, and grammar all are in real-time. The free version covers the basics like identifying grammar and spelling mistakes</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">whereas the Premium version offers a lot more functionality, it detects plagiarism in your content, suggests word choice, or adds fluency to it.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /></span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Features of Grammarly</b></span></h3><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Spelling and Word Suggestion:</b> Grammarly detects basic to advance grammatical errors and also help you why this is an error and suggest to you how you can improve it</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Create a Personal Dictionary:</b> The Grammarly app allows you to add words to your personal dictionary so that the same mistake isn't highlighted every time you run Grammarly.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Different English Style</b>: Check to spell for American, British, Canadian, and Australian English.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Plagiarism:</b> This feature helps you detect if a text has been plagiarized by comparing it with over eight billion web pages.</span></li> <li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Wordiness:</b> This tool will help you check your writing for long and hard-to-read sentences. It also shows you how to shorten sentences so that they are more concise.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Passive Voice:</b> The program also notifies users when passive voice is used too frequently in a document.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Punctuations:</b> This feature flags all incorrect and missing punctuation.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Repetition:</b> The tool provides recommendations for replacing the repeated word.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Proposition:</b> Grammarly identifies misplaced and confused prepositions.</span><center><br /></center> <div id="atContainer-8a426783aef805554f3d96c19f8beeb7"></div> </li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Plugins:</b> It offers Microsoft Word, Microsoft Outlook, and Google Chrome plugins.</span></li></ul><p></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /></span></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">What is ProWritingAid?</span></h2><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">ProWritingAid is a style and grammar checker for content creators and writers. It helps to optimize word choice, punctuation errors, and common grammar mistakes, providing detailed reports to help you improve your writing. </span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">ProWritingAid can be used as an add-on to WordPress, Gmail, and Google Docs. The software also offers helpful articles, videos, quizzes, and explanations to help improve your writing.</span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Features of ProWriting Aid</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Here are some key features of ProWriting Aid:</span></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Grammar checker and spell checker:</b> This tool helps you to find all grammatical and spelling errors.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Find repeated words:</b>  The tool also allows you to search for repeated words and phrases in your content.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Context-sensitive style suggestions:</b>  You can find the exact style of writing you intend and suggest if it flows well in your writing.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Check the readability of your content:</b> Pro Writing Aid helps you identify the strengths and weaknesses of your article by pointing out difficult sentences and paragraphs.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Sentence Length: </b>It also indicates the length of your sentences.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Check Grammatical error:</b> It also checks your work for any grammatical errors or typos, as well.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Overused words:</b> As a writer, you might find yourself using the same word repeatedly. ProWritingAid's overused words checker helps you avoid this lazy writing mistake.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Consistency:</b> Check your work for inconsistent usage of open and closed quotation marks.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Echoes:</b> Check your writing for uniformly repetitive words and phrases.</span></li></ul><p></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Difference between Grammarly and Pro-Writing Aid</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Grammarly</b> and <b>ProWritingAid</b> are well-known grammar-checking software. However, if you're like most people who can't decide which to use, here are some different points that may be helpful in your decision.</span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Grammarly vs ProWritingAid</span></h3><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Grammarly </b>is a writing enhancement tool that offers suggestions for grammar, vocabulary, and syntax whereas <b>ProWritingAid</b> offers world-class grammar and style checking, as well as advanced reports to help you strengthen your writing.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Grammarly</b> provides Android and IOS apps whereas <b>ProWritingAid</b> doesn't have a mobile or IOS app.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Grammarly</b> offers important suggestions about mistakes you've made whereas <b>ProWritingAid</b>  shows more suggestions than Grammarly but all recommendations are not accurate</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Grammarly</b> has a more friendly UI/UX whereas the ProWritingAid interface is not friendly as Grammarly.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Grammarly</b> is an accurate grammar checker for non-fiction writing whereas <b>ProWritingAid</b> is an accurate grammar checker for fiction writers.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Grammarly</b> finds grammar and punctuation mistakes, whereas <b>ProWritingAid</b> identifies run-on sentences and fragments.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Grammarly</b> provides 24/7 support via submitting a ticket and sending emails. <b>ProWritingAid’s</b> support team is available via email, though the response time is approximately 48 hours.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Grammarly</b> offers many features in its free plan, whereas<b> ProWritingAid</b> offers some basic features in the free plan.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Grammarly </b>does not offer much feedback on big picture writing; <b>ProWritingAid</b> offers complete feedback on big picture writing.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Grammarly</b> is a better option for accuracy, whereas <b>ProWritingAid</b> is better for handling fragmented sentences and dialogue. It can be quite useful for fiction writers.</span></li></ul><p></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">ProWritingAid VS Grammarly: Pricing Difference</span></h2><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">ProWritingAid comes with three pricing structures. The full-year cost of ProWritingAid is $79, while its lifetime plans cost $339. You also can opt for a monthly plan of $20.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Grammarly offers a Premium subscription for $30/month for a monthly plan  $20/month for quarterly and $12/month for an annual subscription.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The Business plan costs $12.50 per month for each member of your company.</span></li></ul><p></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">ProWritingAid vs Grammarly – Pros and Cons</span></h2><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Grammarly Pros</span></h3><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">It allows you to fix common mistakes like grammar and spelling.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Offers most features in the free plan</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Allows you to edit a document without affecting the formatting.</span></li><li><span Comfortaa;">Plagiarism checker (paid version)</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Proofread your writing and correct all punctuation, grammar, and spelling errors.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Allows you to make changes to a document without altering its formatting.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Helps users improve vocabulary</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">User-friendly interface</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Browser extensions and MS word improve your style.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Enhance the readability of your sentence</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Free mobile apps </span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Offers  free version</span></li></ul><p></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Grammarly Cons</span></h3><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Supports only English </span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Customer support only via email</span></li><li><span Comfortaa;">Plagiarism checker is only available in a premium plan</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Doesn’t offer a free trial</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">No refund policy</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The free version is ideal for basic spelling and grammatical mistakes, but it does not correct advanced writing issues.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Some features are not available for Mac.</span></li></ul><p></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">ProwritingAid Pros</span></h3><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">It offers more than 20 different reports to help you improve your writing.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Less expensive than other grammar checkers.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">This tool helps you strengthen your writing style as it offers big-picture feedback.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">ProWritingAid has a life plan with no further payments required.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Compatible with Google Docs!</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Prowritingaid works on both Windows and Mac.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">They offer more integrations than most tools.</span></li></ul><p></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">ProWritingAid Cons</span></h3><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Editing can be a little more time-consuming when you add larger passages of text.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">ProWritingAid currently offers no mobile app for Android or iOS devices.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Plagiarism checker is only available in premium plans.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">All recommendations are not accurate</span></li></ul><p></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Summarizing the Ginger VS Grammarly: My Recommendation</span></h2><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">As both writing assistants are great in their own way, you need to choose the one that suits you best.</span></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">For example, go for Grammarly  if you are a non-fiction writer</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Go for ProWritingAid if you are a fiction writer.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">ProWritingAid is better at catching errors found in long-form content. However, Grammarly is more suited to short blog posts and other similar tasks.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">ProWritingAid helps you clean up your writing by checking for style, structure, and content while Grammarly focuses on grammar and punctuation.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Grammarly has a more friendly UI/UX whereas; ProWritingAid offers complete feedback on big picture writing.</span></li></ul><p></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Both ProWritingAid and Grammarly are awesome writing tools, without a doubt. but as per my experience, Grammarly is a winner here because Grammarly helps you to review and edit your content. Grammarly highlights all the mistakes in your writing within seconds of copying and pasting the content into Grammarly’s editor or using the software’s native feature in other text editors.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Not only does it identify tiny grammatical and spelling errors, it tells you when you overlook punctuations where they are needed. And, beyond its plagiarism-checking capabilities, Grammarly helps you proofread your content. Even better, the software offers a free plan that gives you access to some of its features.</span></p><p><br /></p><p><br /></p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://techncruncher.blogspot.com/2022/03/prowritingaid-vs-grammarly-which.html" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9678"> <h2>#9678. Cognizant is putting 25,000+ people on Claude. Here's what's confirmed</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://dev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/articles/3otvb2z646ytpt1hl2rv.jpg" alt="Cognizant is putting 25,000+ people on Claude. Here's what's confirmed" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Cognizant announced on Nov 10 that it's committing more than 25,000 professionals to a new unit, the Claude Frontier Capability Group. The job is helping enterprise clients put Anthropic's Claude into production.</p> <p>CEO Ravi Kumar S said "we are putting more than 25,000 of our people on Claude." Anthropic's chief commercial officer Paul Smith described the same thing as Cognizant "committing more than 25,000 people to help their customers put Claude to work."</p> <p>Alongside the unit, Cognizant introduced a managed services offering. Cognizant runs and maintains Claude-powered systems for clients. The package combines dedicated staff, licensed Claude access and Cognizant's own software, including something it calls its AI Delivery Operating System. The pitch is more predictable AI spend plus security and governance controls. No commercial terms were disclosed.</p> <p>44,000+ Cognizant employees trained or certified on Claude 26,000+ Claude certifications across the company Claude-powered agents will be used to modernize legacy and mainframe systems</p> <p>Cognizant also shared client results, like a pharma manufacturer cutting troubleshooting from 90-120 minutes to 10-15, and an insurer speeding up some operational processes 40-60%. Those figures are Cognizant's own and haven't been independently verified.</p> <p>One thing worth saying plainly. Some coverage frames this as Cognizant moving away from traditional engineer staffing. I couldn't find that in the announcement or the reporting. What's confirmed is a large dedicated Claude team and a managed services model. Whether it changes how Cognizant staffs everything else is an open question.</p> <p>For devs, the practical read is that Claude, MCP and agent tooling are becoming a standard skill in services work, and Cognizant isn't the only one. HCLTech signed its own Anthropic partnership in October, per Analytics India Magazine.</p> <p>Analytics India Magazine: https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news/cognizant-commits-25000-professionals-to-deploy-claude-in-enterprises Yahoo Finance (press release): https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/cognizant-establishes-25-000-person-151221219.html BW People: https://www.bwpeople.in/article/cognizant-deploys-25-000-professionals-for-anthropic-s-claude-633398</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails.
