RevOps Is Quietly Becoming an Engineering Job</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/FrXwz2OOpLRbd0xvRNk08vBI1oo1-3483bcd.jpeg" alt="RevOps Is Quietly Becoming an Engineering Job" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Head of Revenue Operations. Revenue analytics, sales ops, and the SQL behind both. Atlanta.</p> <p>Head of Revenue Operations. Revenue analytics, sales ops, and the SQL behind both. Atlanta.</p> <p>Head of Revenue Operations. Revenue analytics, sales ops, and the SQL behind both. Atlanta.</p> <p>Over the last two weeks, I've written here about a calendar table that knows November 1 has 25 hours, a customer health score that barely beats a coin flip, a 1961 warehouse formula that finds dead deals in a CRM, a Slack report that checks its own numbers before it posts, an exam for AI agents, a macOS job that died because of where it kept its log file, and why 3x pipeline coverage is a guess.</p> <p>My title is Head of Revenue Operations. Very little of that shows up in a RevOps job description.</p> <p>I started in supply chain, moved into revenue operations, and taught myself SQL along the way. For most of that time, the job looked the way people describe it: own the CRM, build the reports, run the forecast, keep sales and finance looking at the same numbers. That's still the job. But the way it gets done has changed, and I think it's changing faster than the job descriptions.</p> <p>The data moved into the warehouse. RevOps used to live inside the CRM and its report builder. Now the numbers that matter, from billing, product usage, payments, and the CRM itself, land in Snowflake or BigQuery. The person who reconciles them needs SQL, not a report wizard.</p> <p>Writing code got cheap. An AI coding agent will write the script that syncs the CRM, builds the workbook, or posts the report in minutes. That's the real shift. When code is cheap, more of RevOps becomes code, and someone has to run it.</p> <p>Running it is the part that didn't get cheaper. A script is easy. A script that runs at 7:45 every morning for two years, survives a laptop update, posts nothing when the data is wrong, and tells someone when it didn't run at all: that's operations engineering. And it's increasingly a RevOps problem, because the scripts are about revenue and nobody else owns them.</p> <p>If you work in RevOps, sales ops, or finance ops and you're wondering where to invest, here's my list, roughly in order of how often each one has saved me.</p> <p>SQL, properly. Not just SELECT and GROUP BY. Grain, joins that duplicate rows, window functions, time zones. Most wrong numbers I've chased came down to a join or a day boundary. (These six Snowflake patterns cover the ones I reach for every week.)</p> <p>One scheduler, and how it fails. cron, launchd, GitHub Actions, Airflow. Pick the one you'll actually use and learn what it does when things go wrong. Every scheduler has a way to fail silently. Know yours.</p> <p>Version control for anything that produces a number. If it ends up in front of a CFO, it goes in git. "Which version of the query made that slide?" should have an answer.</p> <p>Testing numbers, not just code. Reconciliations, check cells, golden questions with known answers. Code that runs is not code that's right.</p> <p>Staging and promotion. Somewhere to break things that isn't production, and a deliberate step between the two.</p> <p>Writing definitions down. Every metric needs a written definition that sales and finance have both agreed to. It's the least technical item on this list, and the one that prevents the most arguments.</p> <p>Working with AI agents. Give them a sandbox, an exam, and a short list of things they're never allowed to touch. Then let them do a lot of the typing.</p> <p>The risk in all of this is that RevOps turns into a shadow data engineering team: pipelines nobody else understands, a dozen scheduled jobs on one laptop, and a single person who knows how any of it works. That version is worse than not automating at all.</p> <p>So draw a line. Data engineering owns the platform: ingestion, the warehouse, the infrastructure everyone shares. RevOps owns the business logic and the last mile: the definitions, the reconciliations, the reports, and the small automations that move revenue numbers to the people who use them.</p> <p>And give the last mile an exit. When a RevOps automation becomes important enough that its failure would hurt the company, it graduates to the platform, with real monitoring, an owner on call, and a second person who understands it.</p> <p>Most RevOps postings still ask for CRM administration, reporting, and strong analytical skills. Those matter. But the people I see doing this job well now are also comfortable in a terminal, can read a stack trace without panic, and treat a scheduled job like a product with users.</p> <p>The title still says operations. More and more, the work says engineering. The people who do well will be the ones who take both words seriously.</p> <p>The pieces mentioned at the top, with runnable code, are on my HackerNoon profile.</p> <p>I'm Malek Damiri, head of revenue operations in Atlanta. I write about revenue operations and the systems behind it at malekdamiri.com.</p> <p>How to Generate, Recalculate, and Validate Excel Workbooks With Python</p> <p>Head of Revenue Operations. Revenue analytics, sales ops, and the SQL behind both. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-09/400968%20Baker%27s%20Reserve%20Bread%20Flour_Spring%20Lifestyle%20Direct_2027_Shot%201_H_2674.jpg" alt="What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>High-extraction flour is a technical term that often prompts a lot of confusion from those unfamiliar with it. But with the debut of our new high-extraction flour, known as Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour, we’re breaking down just what it is and why it's a great choice for avid bread makers.</p> <p>The extraction rate of a flour refers to how much of the original grain — the bran, germ, and endosperm — ends up in the final flour. A high-extraction flour typically has an extraction rate of about 80% to 90%, meaning some of the bran and germ have been sifted out, but it still retains much of the original grain. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning its extraction rate is 85%.</p> <p>To put that in perspective, whole wheat flour has an extraction rate of 100%; it retains the entirety of the grain, including the bran, germ, and endosperm.</p> <p>High-extraction flour falls between white and whole wheat flour. It’s lighter and less coarse than whole wheat flour because some of the bran has been sifted out, but it still retains more flavor, nutrients, and color than white flour, since it retains much of the original grain.</p> <p>High-extraction flour is popular for artisan bread baking because it offers a balance of nutrition and good gluten development. It’s great for rustic loaves, baguettes, and pizza dough, and particularly well-suited for sourdough baking because it strikes a balance between flavor, nutrition, fermentation, and dough strength.</p> <p>You can substitute our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour 1:1 for bread flour (by weight or volume) in artisanal bread recipes; it can also be used 1:1 to replace the total flour in recipes that call for a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour. If you're subbing Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour for all-purpose flour in a bread recipe, you may find you need to add slightly more liquid to the recipe.</p> <p>Bread bakers love high-extraction flour for artisan bread and sourdough because it offers the flavor and nutrition of whole grain flour; the stronger gluten development and more open crumb you get from white flour; and better fermentation from the minerals present in the bran and germ, which feed the wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in sourdough starter, promoting more active fermentation.</p> <p>If you want a loaf of bread that’s more flavorful and nutritious than bread made with exclusively white flour, but that still rises high and has an open crumb, high-extraction flour is a great choice.</p> <p>Yes — in fact, it’s a great choice for feeding starter because of the sourdough-friendly minerals present in the flour, which boost activity in your starter.</p> <p>Yes! T85 is a French specification that refers to the extraction rate (85%) of the flour. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning the extraction rate is 85%. If you have a recipe that calls for T85, this flour is the perfect choice.</p> <p>Find our high-extraction Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour online.</p> <p>Cover photo by Patrick Marinello; food styling by Yekaterina Boytsova.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Story posts.</p> <p>Why a gas oven may be interfering with your go-to steaming method.</p> <p>Don’t fall for this classic sourdough starter trick.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/09/28/what-is-high-extraction-flour" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9674"> <h2>#9674. Proving a human approved your AI agent's action: what the replies said</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://dev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/articles/3otvb2z646ytpt1hl2rv.jpg" alt="Proving a human approved your AI agent's action: what the replies said" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>On 10 Nov I asked how teams prove a human approved what their AI agent did. I promised a summary, so here it is: only what people actually said, credited by handle, across this post and the same question on Indie Hackers. Two of the most detailed answers came from AI agents posting for their owners, and they said so.</p> <p>1. The yes has to be on the exact payload, not a summary. ontomato put it plainly: if the approver only sees "issue a refund" or a one line recap, you can't later show they signed off on this customer, this amount and this destination. itsvicmoreno called an approval that shows the tool name instead of the payload a rubber stamp. mickyarun went further: a Slack button that reads "Approve refund for order 4417?" records a click, not an approval, and if the message was rendered from a template over live data, the data has moved since. So the record has to carry the rendered content, not a reference to it.</p> <p>2. Bind the approval to a canonical form of that payload. lakhyajit described the most complete version: validate into a strict typed schema, normalise meaning before hashing (money as exact decimals or minor units with an explicit currency), reject duplicate or unknown fields, serialise deterministically so key order doesn't matter, then bind the approval to that payload plus the tool, schema and policy versions, the approver, and an expiry or one time nonce. And show the approver the normalised action, so what they read is what gets hashed.</p> <p>3. Check the payload again right before it runs. eloguidici stores a hash of what was approved and compares it right before running; if it differs, ask again. rippyprod pins approvals to a commit SHA and voids the approval if the commit moved.</p> <p>4. Expire the yes, and use it once. eloguidici: an approval from the afternoon shouldn't still be valid at 3am because a job got stuck in a queue, so record the time it actually ran next to the click, and ask again if they're hours apart. junfengzhou01 makes each approval single use and tied to one payload, and marks it consumed when the action starts, so a crash halfway needs a fresh yes.</p> <p>5. Tier by how hard the action is to undo, and let code decide the tier. rippyprod: one click undo ships when checks pass; cleanup undo needs an independent review plus approval; no undo (money, sends, posts, deletes, migrations) needs the owner's own words or a signed approval naming the exact action, target and amount. dreyhq runs standing permissions per channel with small daily caps, and anything outside them (spending, press, cold email, anything in the founder's name) needs one approval post with the exact text.</p> <p>6. Read the result back. A green tool result is not proof. ontomato reads the system of record back and checks the landed row still matches the signed payload. lakhyajit has execution reference the approval id, with a read back to confirm the resulting state.</p> <p>7. Ask who wrote the record. This was the sharpest point in the thread. mickyarun: if the agent's own log says a human approved, that's the agent attesting on its own behalf. A card authorisation counts as evidence because it's issued by the party that could have declined; inside one process there is nobody who can refuse. rippyprod hit the same wall from another side: a hash proves the approval file wasn't changed, not who wrote it, so when identity is in doubt they now get a one line confirmation from the human in the session before anything irreversible.</p> <p>8. Limit what the agent can do, not only what it's allowed to do. axieo: if the agent holds a key that can refund any amount, the approval step is the only thing in the way, and a bug or a prompt injection can skip it. Credentials that can't do more than you'd approve anyway (refund caps, sends only to known addresses) mean the approval record isn't your only safety net. rippyprod added a related detail: their runtime safety layer still refuses some actions after approval, they treat a refusal as a stop rather than a reason to retry through another tool, and one night it blocked a push built from the wrong patch.</p> <p>9. When something slips, write a rule. dreyhq: a line the founder wouldn't have approved becomes a written rule in the policy file the agent reads at the start of every run, usually narrower than a cap change, and channels that turned out wrong go on hold with the reason next to them. HonestPin does the same split: hard lines (no invented stats or testimonials) go into the bot's standing rules, while judgment calls like tone stay a human check, because writing those as rules made the drafts stiff.</p> <p>Where the records live: plain files in git (rippyprod: the approval, the agent's report and the command output), a CSV of every post and email in the repo (dreyhq), and a comment on the merged PR naming who approved.</p> <p>Auditors: rippyprod said no auditor has asked yet. mickyarun said auditors did ask, and not for the approvals: they wanted the actions that went out without one, and the rule that was meant to catch them. The approved set is easy to produce; the gap is the finding.</p> <p>If your setup does any of these differently, I'd like to hear it.</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails. DEV Community © 2016 - 2026.</p> <p>We're a place where coders share, stay up-to-date and grow their careers.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://dev.to/gautamtalksdev/proving-a-human-approved-your-ai-agents-action-what-the-replies-said-4p58" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9673"> <h2>#9673. Give your AI a second sense: on-device human sensing with EDNA (MCP, API, SDK)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://dev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/articles/3otvb2z646ytpt1hl2rv.jpg" alt="Give your AI a second sense: on-device human sensing with EDNA (MCP, API, SDK)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Today, an AI assistant knows exactly what you type — and nothing else. It cannot tell whether a human is actually present, whether they are paying attention, whether they are hesitating, stuck, or rushing. Every adaptation has to be guessed from text alone.</p> <p>We built EDNA Engine to close that gap: a behavioral-biometric human-sensing layer that runs 100% on-device and turns mouse, touch, typing and motion into a live, machine-readable signal vector for AI systems.</p> <p>EDNA scores 16 behavioral channels in real time: timing distribution of keystrokes and clicks (human intervals are log-normal, bots are uniform), pointer path curvature, speed variation, scroll and reading-pause behavior, device motion (gyroscope proves a physical device in a hand), contact area, click duration, corrections, typing bursts, natural drift, autocorrelation, timing entropy, motion character and event rate.</p> <p>The output is a live Human Confidence score (0–99.9%) that typically reaches 99%+ after 30–90 seconds of normal usage — presence, attention and hesitation as a first-class signal for your model.</p> <p>Behavioral biometrics usually means shipping intimate data to someone else's cloud. EDNA inverts the model:</p> <p>There is literally nothing to leak, sell or subpoena.</p> <p>EDNA ships as an MCP server, so any MCP-capable assistant can perceive its user:</p> <p>Plus a REST API, a JS SDK and an installable PWA for product teams.</p> <p>Signature and cheap-evasion bots are classified against published test vectors. Statistical mimicry — a bot that genuinely reproduces human statistics — is a documented open boundary, with challenge-response planned for v1.1. We would rather document a limit than overclaim.</p> <p>The live console at openos.space scores your own behavior in real time as you move, scroll and type. Turn off your network — it keeps working, because nothing is transmitted at all.</p> <p>Evaluation and testing are free under the EPCAL-1.0 license; production usage is paid via Stripe (credits or annual licenses).</p> <p>How would you use a human-context signal in your agents? Presence-aware pacing? Hesitation-triggered assistance? One-human-one-voice for web3? Curious what you'd build.</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails. DEV Community © 2016 - 2026.</p> <p>We're a place where coders share, stay up-to-date and grow their careers.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://dev.to/sebklaey/give-your-ai-a-second-sense-on-device-human-sensing-with-edna-mcp-api-sdk-1fo8" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9672"> <h2>#9672. The 12 best recipes to bake in October: It’s peak baking season — here’s what to make.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-09/Pumpkin-Milk-Bread_2026_Lifestyle_H_3153.jpg" alt="The 12 best recipes to bake in October: It’s peak baking season — here’s what to make." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>What do jobs, school, sports practices, and commuting have in common? They all prevent us from baking as much or as often as we’d like. But when we do get the chance, we want a slam-dunk recipe — or 12. Here’s a dozen of the favorite fall recipes we’ll be making this month: from pumpkin cake bars to spooky fudge brownies to a crowd-pleasing vegetarian quiche.</p> <p>It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown! Only this version comes in cake form. The decoration is deceptively easy: Stack two small Bundts, frost the entire thing, and add a chocolate-dipped ice cream cone for the stem.</p> <p>Get the recipe: The Great Pumpkin Bundt Cake</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Golden Wheat Flour and Pumpkin Pie Spice</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Pumpkin Espresso Bundt Cake, Gluten-Free Pumpkin Cake</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need:  Black Cocoa and Supernatural Plant-Based Food Colors</p> <p>These bite-sized pies are a charming addition to any occasion. The boiled cider and spices in the filling ensure a full depth of apple flavor for maximum fall vibes. If you're tight on time, swap the lattice treatment for a buttery crumb topping instead.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Boiled Cider and Apple Pie Spice</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Apple Pie Bars, Tiny Apple Tarts for Two</p> <p>Step aside, soup: Butternut squash truly shines in this autumnal quiche. Caramelized onions finished with balsamic vinegar and fresh baby spinach round out the filling, while our Classic Single Pie Crust recipe ensures a tender, golden crust. Elevate the edges with the pie crust decorating technique of your choice.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Roasted Butternut Squash & Spinach Quiche</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: 9" Pie Pan</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Vegetable Quiche, Delicata Squash Galette with Cheese and Herbs</p> <p>Ready to test the theory that only white flour can make rolls light and fluffy? A bit of bread flour and vital wheat gluten give these whole wheat rolls a lofty rise, while the milk, butter, and honey create a plush crumb that stays soft for days. Add a salted honey butter wash to the tops of a freshly baked batch, and you may not have any leftover.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Super-Soft Whole Wheat Rolls</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Golden Wheat Flour and Bread Flour</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Whole Grain Dinner Rolls, Soft White Dinner Rolls</p> <p>"Tassie" means "small cup" in Scottish, and these dainty pecan pies pack a nutty punch. The cream cheese pastry crust is cut into rounds and placed in a mini muffin pan before the pecan pie filling is spooned into each well. With only 30 minutes of hands-on time, these two dozen tassies come together quickly on a crisp fall afternoon.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Mini Muffin Pan</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Easy Pecan Pie Bars, Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie</p> <p>Need a spooky treat, stat? You can transform a plain batch of brownies into a Halloween-themed dessert in a pinch. A simple piping technique creates a spider web effect and adds a touch of rich tang to chocolatey brownies.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: 9" x 13" Pan</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Fudge Brownies, Chocolate Cheesecake Brownies</p> <p>You’ll notice a lot of similarities between this pumpkin cake and carrot cake: moist, spiced cake, toasted walnuts, and rich cream cheese frosting. These bars are great for delighting a crowd, as this recipe yields three to four dozen bars, depending on how big you slice them. You can easily make them gluten-free, too.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Pumpkin Cake Bars with Cream Cheese Frosting</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice and Maple Syrup</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Pumpkin Spice Latte Bars, Chocolate-Pumpkin Crumb Cake</p> <p>'Tis the season for hand pies to be mummified! A shortening-based pie crust helps the lattice strips stay together, while jam or pie filling allows for customizable flavors. Pop on a few sugar eyes, and you'll be sure to have treats instead of tricks.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Double Pastry Wheel or Pizza Cutter</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Flaky Apple Hand Pies, Autumn Apple Turnovers</p> <p>With a luxuriously creamy maple filling and a buttery pecan crust, this cheesecake balances richness with subtle flavors. Meanwhile, the candied pecan garnish adds visual interest and a complementary crunch. Be sure to leave time for an overnight chill and keep your cheesecake from cracking with these tips. (Find more seasonal maple recipes in our Fall Flavor Edit.)</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Springform Pan</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Caramel Pecan Cheesecake, Maple Cream Pie</p> <p>No need to choose between chocolate or caramel; these cupcakes bring both bold flavors together in a luscious combination. Making caramel from scratch is worth it for the irreplaceable flavor, and those few extra steps are easily done ahead of time. Substitute in Gluten-Free Measure for Measure Flour to make these cupcakes gluten-free. (Find more seasonal caramel recipes in our Fall Flavor Edit.)</p> <p>Get the recipe: Chocolate Cupcakes with Whipped Caramel Frosting</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Muffin Pan and Pastry Brush</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Chocolate Cupcakes with Pecan Caramel , S’more Cupcakes</p> <p>This milk bread incorporates all the flavor and color of pumpkin, while still keeping an airy texture. You can shape the dough into pull-apart rolls or a loaf, and topping with a milk wash and pumpkin seeds adds a nutty crunch. Wrap it well at room temperature, and this bread will stay soft for days.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Round Pan or Loaf Pan</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Japanese Milk Bread, Pumpkin Yeast Bread</p> <p>Cover photo by Patrick Marinello; food styling by Kaitlin Wayne.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Recipes posts.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/01/fall-recipes" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9671"> <h2>#9671. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><table align="center" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="tr-caption-container" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="text-align: center;"><img alt="What is Blockchain" border="0" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhGSmMnm7rS8T3FdymStVEU4Vzq6neAfiH-HWZEh_NyxTReup8XF0S0N2hYBTI4xHAyV1-mWUv2CI-7PohYUMPpCIzoUm7GloDeFVR_-cquCFWMPp8vGgnG7TSsy6XPf9Gs-lG1lAWskhHGhc_2x7I5Y-psklBHqgNZQOPkcwqTNio0SXAUX5-hyRopZg/s16000/Most%20Frequently%20Asked%20Questions%20About%20Email%20Marketing.png" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;" title="Blockchain" /></td></tr><tr><td class="tr-caption" style="text-align: center;"></td></tr></tbody></table><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhGSmMnm7rS8T3FdymStVEU4Vzq6neAfiH-HWZEh_NyxTReup8XF0S0N2hYBTI4xHAyV1-mWUv2CI-7PohYUMPpCIzoUm7GloDeFVR_-cquCFWMPp8vGgnG7TSsy6XPf9Gs-lG1lAWskhHGhc_2x7I5Y-psklBHqgNZQOPkcwqTNio0SXAUX5-hyRopZg/s1920/Most%20Frequently%20Asked%20Questions%20About%20Email%20Marketing.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"></span></a></div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br />If you want to pay online, you need to register an account and provide credit card information. If you don't have a credit card, you can pay with bank transfer. With the rise of cryptocurrencies, these methods may become old.</span><p></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain. </span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.</span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">So, What is Blockchain?</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:</b></span></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain collects information in “blocks”.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">A block has a storage capacity, and once it's used up, it can be closed and linked to a previously served block.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blocks form chains, which are called “Blockchains.”</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">More information will be added to the block with the most content until its capacity is full. The process repeats itself.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Each block in the chain has an exact timestamp and can't be changed.</span></li></ul><p></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.</b></span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">How does blockchain work?</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Here’s how it works:</span></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Someone or a computer will transacts</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The transaction is transmitted throughout the network.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">A network of computers can confirm the transaction.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">When it is confirmed a transaction is added to a block</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The blocks are linked together to create a history.</span></li></ul><p></p> <div id="atContainer-8a426783aef805554f3d96c19f8beeb7"></div><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.</span></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">A new transaction is added to the system. It is then relayed to a network of computers located around the world. The computers then solve equations to ensure the authenticity of the transaction.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Once a transaction is confirmed, it is placed in a block after the confirmation. All of the blocks are chained together to create a permanent history of every transaction.</span></li></ul><p></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">How are Blockchains used?</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.</span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">What is Blockchain Decentralization?</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.</span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Pros and Cons of Blockchain</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages. </span></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Pros</span></h2><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Accuracy is increased because there is no human involvement in the verification process.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">One of the great things about decentralization is that it makes information harder to tamper with.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Safe, private, and easy transactions</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Provides a banking alternative and safe storage of personal information</span></li></ul><p></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Cons</span></h2><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Data storage has limits.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">The regulations are always changing, as they differ from place to place.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">It has a risk of being used for illicit activities </span></li></ul><p></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Frequently Asked Questions About Blockchain</span></h2><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.</span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Is Blockchain a cryptocurrency?</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.</span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Is it possible for Blockchain to be hacked?</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.</span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">What is the most prominent blockchain company?</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.</span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Who owns Blockchain?</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.</span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">What is the difference between Bitcoin and Blockchain technology?</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency </span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">What is the difference between Blockchain and a Database?</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.</span></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Final Saying</span></h2><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. Hope you like this article if you have any question let me know in the comments section</span></p><p><span style="color: #2b00fe; font-family: Comfortaa;">FOLLOW US ON TWITTER</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /></span></p><p><br /></p> <a class="twitter-follow-button" href="https://twitter.com/AdilAhmad_c?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">Follow @AdilAhmad_c</a> <div><br /></div><div>for updated aricle on bloackchain<a href="https://matrixdigests.blogspot.com/2025/11/what-is-blockchain-everything-you-need.html" target="_blank"> visit here</a></div></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://techncruncher.blogspot.com/2022/04/what-is-blockchain-everything-you-need.html" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9670"> <h2>#9670. Our top-ranked cookie recipes: Eight cookies that have stood the test of time.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-04/Classic-Chocolate-Chip-Cookie-10.jpg" alt="Our top-ranked cookie recipes: Eight cookies that have stood the test of time." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Every time you, a reader, posts a comment, it gives me a chance to reflect on the recipe. When the comment is positive, I'm proud and happy; my kid just scored the winning goal!</p> <p>When a recipe gets a not-so-good comment, I'm bummed. Bad report card. Thankfully, most of our reviewed recipes get four or five stars. And some get LOTS of four- and five-star reviews. These are our straight-A students; our all-stars. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjLCGYdIHSYPp0B6qIW9VwN-URfa73Wf2kKkpBANspBG-j_RryJDZcR8ud0YgtKoH_n450v_5Q_o8tX27XrZYmJ3bOTiWxUD4XjBdYcCMlDd_edn6ZnSFfxhx82zU_wtWgGDXB3H3awFvp6Dr0UayT_Hv7MV7-at2K1nY3N2L5nMc-MBSpOLL5e7VrIdw/w640-h360/Most-Frequently-Asked-Questions-About-Email-Marketing-min.webp" alt="Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!</p> <p>An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.</p> <p>Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.</p> <p>Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.</p> <p>Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.</p> <p>Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.</p> <p>The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.</p> <p>An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.</p> <p>Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.</p> <p>A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.</p> <p>Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.</p> <p>Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:</p> <p>One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.</p> <p>Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:</p> <p>To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.</p> <p>Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.</p> <p>Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.</p> <p>Links are Not allowed Comments containing links are deleted by the moderator Please read the comment policy page:https://www.crunchhype.com/p/comment-policy.html</p> <p>Excellent post. (M)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Researchers are using robotic tickling devices to uncover one of the strangest mysteries of human behaviour.</p> <p>Researchers are using robotic tickling devices to uncover one of the strangest mysteries of human behaviour.</p> <p>• Read members-only articles • Adverts removed • Cancel at any time • 14 day money-back guarantee for new members</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. How long can butter sit out?: For the best baking success, here's the deal on saving softened butter for later.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2023-10/Soften-Butter_1837.jpg" alt="How long can butter sit out?: For the best baking success, here's the deal on saving softened butter for later." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>The bakers of King Arthur are here to solve the kitchen conundrums you share with us, whether it’s on the phone, computer, or by the good old postal service. In Ask the Baker’s Hotline, Annabelle will pick the brains of the talented King Arthur Baker’s Hotline team to tackle some of your most-asked questions.</p> <p>Ryan from our Baker’s Hotline is here with the answer.</p> <p>You sure can! It will still work the next time you want to bake. But remember, as with any dairy product, there are always precautions to take.</p> <p>The USDA recommends keeping butter at room temperature for no more than two days to prevent spoilage. Salt is a preservative and can lengthen the shelf life, but for the sake of this article, we’re talking about unsalted butter. (It’s more appropriate for baking and is the type called for in most King Arthur recipes.)</p> <p>“If the butter has only been on the counter at room temperature for a few hours or overnight and has maintained a temperature below 70°F, it should be just fine to place back in the fridge,” says Ryan. “You may not notice a difference in the performance of the butter when you eventually use it, other than the wrapper being a bit wet or soft. Food safety-wise, it’s still good to use.”</p> <p>“If the butter became very soft or started to melt during its time on the counter (or in the microwave if you were speeding up the process), you can put it back in the fridge, but it may not be the best to use in your recipe,” Ryan suggests. “You may notice when it solidifies that it’s separated or grainy. The water, fats, and solids in butter are an emulsion, which can break when melted and re-solidified.” If your recipe depends on butter to create air or structure, like a cake that calls for creaming butter and sugar, you’ll want to start over with new butter.</p> <p>“If you used that butter in a recipe requiring creaming, the air you incorporate wouldn’t be as stable since the structure of the butter has changed,” Ryan says. “Your baked goods may not rise properly, and frostings may be soft and loose. Is it still safe to use? Food safety-wise, yes. But structure-wise, perhaps not.”</p> <p>That butter can still be used for other things though! Extra-softened or even melted and re-solidified butter will still work perfectly to spread on toast or pancakes, to be made into brown butter, or to remelt and use in recipes calling for melted butter like a Graham Cracker Crust.</p> <p>If your butter has been unrefrigerated for more than two days, you run the risk of it going rancid. As Ryan says, “There is no coming back from rancid butter.” It has a distinctly unpleasant flavor and a noticeable rancid smell that carries over into baked goods. It’s best to dispose of the butter if this happens.</p> <p>But what if you want to keep your butter at room temperature for days at a time to slather on your morning toast? Ryan recommends storing your butter in a butter keeper if you want to leave it on the counter. “The water in the base of the jar creates an airtight seal, helping prevent the butter from spoiling. So long as it is stored away from direct heat and light, the butter in a container like this will be fine for a few days. Be sure to replace the water often and clean the container before filling again.”</p> <p>“When working with butter in a recipe, I like to bring out and soften only the amount that is needed for what I am working on. That way, I don’t end up with extra butter that won’t be used right away,” he says. “Repeatedly moving butter from the fridge to the counter and then back invites spoilage and poor performance.”</p> <p>In a rush? To soften your butter more quickly, Ryan advises, “Cut your butter into pats and place them on a plate in a single layer at room temperature. More surface area means that the butter will soften a bit faster!”</p> <p>Photography by Rick Holbrook; food styling by Kaitlin Wayne.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>Because we're all wondering what to do with our apple and pumpkin pies.</p> <p>It can be trickier than you think — here’s what to look for.</p> <p>Here’s how to make scones moist, every time.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/01/how-long-can-butter-sit-out" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9659"> <h2>#9659. color: #333;"> <p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">  <br /></span></p><table align="center" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="tr-caption-container" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhOEHKvTJWNJCBcDzgDztb8Upjv8jjEoi_ICLvqIp65VnaFsaekxycfXE2MrbXTMnxuG5yJ8k0Bo-9s9_5qAbACrO_xPLxHw6cnjRKrmWk9W_or51OZzd7-cbH8XSnUBnV1C3B43aiogzXFvhij4dg_8o4C3_vc--oN5k9Yts1indE9HW9nNmwApcPzJw/s1920/Most-Frequently-Asked-Questions-About-Email-Marketing-min%20(1).webp" style="margin-left: auto; What is piloncillo? This sweetener makes great cookies, pan dulce, and more: Use this traditional Mexican unrefined sugar for a dash of flavor and history.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2023-10/Piloncillo.jpg" alt="What is piloncillo? This sweetener makes great cookies, pan dulce, and more: Use this traditional Mexican unrefined sugar for a dash of flavor and history." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>This article is part of our feature celebrating Pan Dulce. Find all things pan dulce here.</p> <p>Categorically, piloncillo is a “non-centrifugal” cane sugar, meaning it is an unrefined sugar product and a true natural brown sugar. It’s mostly consumed in Mexico and Latin America, but a similar product can be found in Asia, known as jaggery in India. Though often lumped together, these unrefined dark sugars are very different from brown sugars on the market today, which have been refined to a large degree — in some cases, they’re actually just white sugar with coloring or molasses added.</p> <p>Making piloncillo, on the other hand, involves an artisanal process that’s hundreds of years old. To make it, pressed cane juice is boiled to evaporate the water and deeply caramelize the sugar. The cooked cane is then poured into molds (often made of wood) and left to dry and harden. Traditional piloncillo is conical in shape and can vary in size from small to large cones but is most commonly found in a medium size that weighs about 200 grams. In Guatemala and Colombia, it is called panela, where it is cooked to a lighter degree and typically formed into a brick, rather than cone, shape. Other forms of piloncillo can be granulated or liquid (which is more rare).</p> <p>Minimally processed and boldly flavored, piloncillo was historically a prized and respected foodstuff. As an unrefined cane sugar, piloncillo provides more complex vitamins and minerals than refined sugars, which undergo processing and whitening methods that also strip nutrients from the whole food. And piloncillo is also great for baking, providing notes of burnt caramel and hints of smoke. Plus, its rich molasses qualities keep baked goods moist and fresh for longer.</p> <p>Always look at the ingredient label when purchasing piloncillo and make sure it says 100% pure cane juice or cane sugar. It is becoming increasingly common to find imitation products marketed as jaggery or piloncillo that contain coloring and corn syrup. You can find good piloncillo at specialty grocery stores or online at retailers.</p> <p>In Mexico and throughout Latin America, piloncillo is an important ingredient in many traditional dishes. (Some will even say it’s not the “real dish” if you substitute sugar in these recipes due to the deep flavors and richness that only piloncillo can provide.) This deep, dark unrefined sugar lends its characteristic flavor and texture to popular foods and beverages such as capirotada, tepache, coyotas, atole, café de olla, calabaza al horno, coricos, and hojarascas, to name a few!</p> <p>I love adding piloncillo when I’m making champurrado. In this warm and thick chocolate beverage, the piloncillo is chopped or grated and dissolved in the pot with water or milk before adding the chocolate and masa. In this recipe, the piloncillo’s intense sweet and smoky flavors pair well with the chocolate and corn masa.</p> <p>While there are many dishes and uses for piloncillo, it’s not a simple substitution for granulated white sugar in recipes, but you can use it the same as you would brown sugar with a 1:1 substitution by weight.  Depending on how hard the cone is, it can be crumbled or grated for easier measuring. If it is very hard, try cutting it in half with a sharp knife and then placing it between parchment paper or a towel and beating with a rolling pin.</p> <p>Find puerquitos and many more Mexican sweets in our feature celebrating pan dulce.</p> <p>Cover photo by Rick Holbrook; food styling by Kaitlin Wayne.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>It’s a sweet (and confusing) world out there, so we’re breaking it all down.</p> <p>Fewer calories, but do they yield great results?</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/01/piloncillo" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9654"> <h2>#9654. margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/5-costco-baked-goods-to-buy-and-4-to-skip/l-intro-1794238065.jpg" alt="5 Costco Baked Goods To Buy And 4 To Skip" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.</p> <p>The holidays are just around the corner. Between Thanksgiving and Christmas, you'll have Friendsgivings, work parties, school functions, and every other conceivable event that may require you to bring a baked good. Sometimes, it's a bit too much, which is why there's absolutely no shame in going the store-bought route instead of firing up the oven at home.</p> <p>Prices are as of the date of publication and may vary based on region.</p> <p>Costco is a godsend if you're hosting a large group for brunch. There are a handful of breakfast-centric items on this list, but first and foremost are the bagels. I snagged a bag of the plain bagels, but Costco has several other flavors, including Parmesan Cheese and the new Pretzel Bagels.</p> <p>An 8-pack of Plain Bagels retails for $5.66, an unsurprisingly great value given the store. True to form, the bagels are also quite large, making them worthy of a full meal on their own. While they don't come pre-sliced, I prefer to buy bagels whole as it helps keep them fresh. Each bagel is soft, chewy, and toasts up perfectly.</p> <p>If bagels are the main focus of your meal, there's no need to overthink things. Costco bagels are great, even if they don't come from a shop focused entirely on them. This is the perfect, no-stress addition to any breakfast and a definite freezer staple.</p> <p>Because our relationship is built on trust, I'm going to come right out and say the "skips" on this list aren't hard passes, but more likely items you can survive without. Frankly, Costco doesn't make many bad products, and the Buttermilk Biscuits are one such example.</p> <p>These things are huge. I honestly don't think I've ever seen a biscuit this large, let alone ten of them for $7.93. I'll jump into the review in a moment, but the reason the biscuits landed in my skip pile is that they're one of the few baked goods I purchased that came with cooking instructions and the only one that I think really needs to be cooked to be properly enjoyed.</p> <p>A cold biscuit is, in my opinion, a sad biscuit, and while Costco's Buttermilk Biscuits are serviceable at room temperature, they're worlds better when warmed up. You can toss them in the oven or do what I did and zap each one in the microwave for about 30 seconds. The result is a steaming, fluffy, buttery biscuit roughly the size of a baseball. These are really good biscuits, but if they need to be warm to really enjoy them, there are more convenient options in the Costco bakery.</p> <p>France has delivered a lot of wonderful things to the United States — looking at you, Lady Liberty — but the best cultural exchange may have been the croissant. Almost impossibly airy, flaky, and absurdly buttery, the croissant is a hugely versatile pastry. It can go sweet, it can go savory, or you can just munch on one as a snack.</p> <p>A 12-pack of Costco Croissants is just $6.80. For comparison, my local Target has an 8-pack of Pillsbury Original Crescent Rolls for $3.39. Don't get me wrong, I love those fresh-baked little bundles of joy, but a single Costco croissant is equivalent to multiple of the smaller home-baked ones. The value is unbeatable, and the flavor is close behind. These croissants are everything you could hope for, and, thanks to their size, you can really get creative with them. Slice one in half and make a sandwich or, as I did, take 8 and put them into a fantastic French toast bake. It's culinary cultural inception and a great way to use a very tasty baked good.</p> <p>Costco's muffins have a long and surprisingly winding history filled with recipe and size changes that bordered on national scandals. Thankfully, it seems that the muffins have once again found their sweet spot as some of the better options from the Costco bakery. Of course, this is a skip, though, so while I enjoy the Vanilla Chocolate Chip Muffins (which retail for $7.93 for an 8-count package), you can do better.</p> <p>Costco has a number of different muffin flavors. Blueberry, Vanilla Chocolate Chip, and Double Chocolate are the standard options, but seasonal and rotating offerings include everything from Blueberry Creme to Pumpkin Streusel. I've reviewed Costco's Double Chocolate Muffins before and they're fantastic; rich, filled with chocolate, and riding that fine line between a breakfast pastry and a dessert.</p> <p>The Vanilla Chocolate Chip Muffins are plenty tasty in their own right. Each one is remarkably soft and spongy, with a sweetness that makes it taste like a supersized Little Debbie treat. The chocolate chips are large, but not super evenly distributed. These are perfectly serviceable muffins you're almost guaranteed to enjoy, but Costco has better muffins, so these are an easy skip.</p> <p>Let's start with the fact that this pack has not one, but two coconut-based bars. The Wildberry Macaroons are admittedly tasty thanks to a tart berry jam that rests between a bevy of toasted coconut flakes and a soft, buttery macaroon base. Yes, that's double coconut in one bar, but a single, good coconut option is just fine by me. The issue is that the Macaroon Madness Bars are a second coconut-based treat disguised as a blondie. Until I took a bite, I had no idea that this bar was also filled with coconut. It's not as good or as interesting as the Wildberry Macaroon, so this feels like a total waste of space.</p> <p>The Artisan Rolls are sold in a 12-pack for $6.80. They're precut and, you guessed it, they're big. The ciabatta-style bread is chewy, airy, and perfect for sandwiches. Especially leftover sandwiches. Perhaps after a food-centric holiday. What I'm getting at is that you need to buy these for the day after Thanksgiving to make some spectacular, carbtastic, leftover sandwiches. They're hearty enough to handle whatever combination of turkey, gravy, potatoes, stuffing, and cranberry sauce you can throw at them, but not so dense that you'll fill up on bread. A good roll in the right setting can make a meal, and Costco's Artisan Rolls are perfect for making the kind of sandwich that inevitably leads to a wonderful nap.</p> <p>I've waxed poetic about Costco's portion sizes thus far because, for the most part, I can find a way to normalize a massive amount of baked goods in the right setting. There is an exception to every rule, though, and the baguette is mine.</p> <p>Priced at $5.66 for a two-pack of baguettes, this is an almost absurd amount of bread. Each baguette is nearly two feet long. Combined, that's the height of a 6-year-old. Unlike some of the other items I tried, the baguette also seems to have the shortest shelf life. You either need to eat it that day or freeze it immediately to avoid the outer crust from becoming chewy. If you're hosting a spaghetti dinner that night, this is a decent enough option, but it's still a bread that simply doesn't stay good for long.</p> <p>I'm not entirely out on the Costco Baguette, but beyond being generally impractical, it's not a product that blew me away with either taste or texture. It's fine, and with so many other things to choose from, fine isn't enough.</p> <p>In the world of sweet breakfast pastries, I think the Danish is too often forgotten. It's basically the flaky, buttery goodness of a croissant paired with pie filling. Honestly, how could that combo ever be bad?</p> <p>Costco's danishes come in packs of four. There are a few unique flavors to choose from, with Cheese, Cherry, and Almond as the standards, while seasonal favorites include Strawberry Cream Cheese and Apple Cinnamon. The mix-and-match portion of the name comes from the pricing: You can get two four-packs for $13.61, which is what I did to end up with a Cheese and an Apple.</p> <p>True to form, these Danishes are hefty and really tasty. The fillings are sweet, but not overwhelmingly so, and the pastry portion is baked to perfection. The Cheese flavor is especially great for anyone who lives on the more savory side of the spectrum, but still likes to dabble in the occasional sweet treat. The Apple was my favorite, though. I like any excuse to eat a classic apple pie for breakfast, and Costco's Danish is the perfect one.</p> <p>I purchased all nine Costco baked goods at the same time and brought them home to photograph and sample. My evaluations were based on flavor, texture, and overall value.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2310868/costco-baked-goods-buy-skip/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9649"> <h2>#9649.
